Weathered wood marks a place of respite in a cold and unfeeling world, where one can numb themselves with stale company and yet more stale drink.
Polished wood and leaf gold marks the office of the steward, manager of the city lord's estate and treasury.
A small swinging anvil sign marks the smithy, where bloodied coin changes hands for hasty repairs and second hand weaponry.
A small swinging sign engraved with a goblet marks a common dining hall, it may lack the majesty of a city tavern, but it serves as a place to eat and rest in relative safety.
In a world of disease and violence a bathhouse is a rare spot of respite, where one can wash away exhausion and sin alike in warm, perfumed waters.

A rugged white banner stitched with a blood-red sparrow, the mark of the Mercenary Guild. A loose confederation of smaller mercenary companies and independent contractors, they can be trusted as far as you can spend your gold.

Alone against a black sky and crimson field sits a white oak, regal and proud. The craftsmanship is exquisite and the banner is made of fine linen, but the heraldry is unfamiliar to you. Perhaps a forgotten dynasty or mercenary company?

On a black field a fearsome serpent coils, the heraldry of the barony of House Lindwurm, 'Our Work is Eternal' went their house motto. Crushed by the taxes of the city lord's ancestors, the barony of Lord Lindwurm was forced to abandon its lands and flee to the capital city of Kingsfield. Now their estate is occupied by the wretches of the realm, squatting in the ruins of their glory.

Golden tools gleam against the blue of the oceans these craftsmen cross in their trade and works. The proud flag of the artificer guild, a collection of artisans and craftsmen who work together for shared profit and protection. In some cities their legal rights rival that of the petty nobility.
A dark drape of fabric, a featureless decoration for those too cowardly to mark their heraldry.
An old shield mounted on the wall, its heraldry damaged and faded by time. No longer able to serve its purpose in combat, its function is now decorative.

A sign advertising the services of the Merchant Guild, a widespread alliance of merchants across the world. Here you can hope to earn enough from your spoils to at least break even, if not afford a meal.

Fine silk dyed in deep purple with golden thread in its trim, this banner is the mark of the Sun Cult. Wherever the rays of Astrata touch the world, there may be found her followers, who claim authority over all sects and temples.

Rich red silk trimmed with silver thread marks the banner of the Otavan Orthodoxy, the church of the Creator-God PSYDON which dominates the nation of Otava and sends its Inquisition abroad to root out heresy in its neighbors.

Made by the traveling scholar Johann Grünwald in his travels across the continent, this painting depicts a moonlit night in the wilderness of Grenzelhoft. While there are many replicas of this painting, a few highly prized originals still exist.

Made by the traveling scholar Johann Grünwald in his travels across the lands, this painting depicts a peaceful moonlit lake in the Otavan countryside. A popular piece among the wealthy, even a good replica can fetch a fine price.
A painting of a woman, its frame is weathered and its paint peels from the canvas. Time has not treated this piece well, but it has a certain charm to it.
Prominently fluttering in the breeze you see the sturdy banner of the realm, the heraldry of the city lord's family. Many would be honored to wear these colors in loyal service to the crown.
Prominently fluttering in the breeze you see the sturdy banner of the barony, the heraldry of the local baron. Many would be honored to wear these colors in loyal service to lowtown.

On a plate of silvered metal is draped a banner of deep purple, with the leering face of a crescent moon in its center; the heraldry of Noc has an expression of deep concentration, meant to inspire insight in his acolytes.
A painting of a candelabra and human skull on a covered table, it is a modestly grim yet tasteful piece of art.
A painting of a forest and distant castle shrouded in fog, it gives a feeling of mystery as the mind fills in the details.
A painting of a noble crown atop a book with an apple to its side, it is a simple yet elegant piece on the elements of any good ruler's life.

Frostbite can cause severe burns and tissue damage if untreated, and while warming up can lessen the damage, existing frostbite must be treated. Slice open the patient and apply clamps to prevent bleedout, retract the incision, cut away the dead tissue with a scalpel, then clean the cut before removing your tools and closing up the wound.

Eye surgery is a delicate procedure, requiring focus and skill. Ensure the patient is numbed from pain, then carefully cut at the eye, clamping and retracting for better access. Manipulate the eye with care to remove it, insert the replacement, slice to ensure a flow of healthy blood to the new eyes, then clean and close the site.

When a limb is severed, it must be sutured immediately before bleedout occurs. Once the limb is applied to the stump, the arteries will be re-opened, and you must suture the limb. Use bone forceps to set the limb in place, then forceps to ensure the muscles won't separate once the patient begins to move. Suture to finish.

Toxins can quickly travel through the blood and overwhelm the patient, so the use of leeches has become essential in modern medicine. Regular leeches will drain blood until they are fully engorged, harming the patient if ripped off early. Some students of medical science are gifted with the cheele, a helpful specialized leech which can switch between draining or infusing blood when its stomach is gently pressed on.

As the pump that moves blood through the body, lux naturally accumulates over the heart in layers. With careful practice, it can be scraped off the surface and collected for further use. This will leave the patient weakened, and they should rest properly after volunteering for lux donation.

When the new medical student is confused on how to revive a patient, there may be several causes for a failure to revitalize. Attempt to diagnose your patient if possible, as the issue may be ensanguination, significant bodily trauma, or even sustained oxygen deprivation damage. Rebalance their humors, tend bruises and burns, conduct CPR, and if all else fails ask your mentor for advice.

Fine dark leather boots.
A pair of sturdy riding boots with an iron heel and brass spurs.
Leather boots that reach up to the thighs. Comfortable for both riding and standing in court all dae.
Common shoes for everyday wear by the peasantry.
A humble pair of sandals with adjustable straps that allow a snug fit for almost anyone.

Polished gilbranze platforms, curled about to cradle the feet. Gladiators from an era lost, reborn to serve. These sandals were never meant to march 'pon sands, but to stand tall over the bodies of one's enemies.
Frayed bronze platforms, curled about to cradle the feet. The beaches that these sandals once treaded are no more; pearly sands, long since turnt to glass from the Comet Syon's impact.
Sturdy boots stitched together from tanned leather. They leak a little.
Sturdy boots stitched together from cured leather. Stylish, firm, and sport a satisfying 'squeek' with each step.
A pair of sturdy boots stitched together from cured leather. These are shorter than usual, made for casual wear and dueling.
Boots of outstanding craft, your fragile feet have never felt so protected and comfortable before.

A pair of lightweight snugly fitting boots. They're reinforced along the toes and ankles and offer a measure of protection against missteps and glancing blows during close exchanges, often favoured by duelists and other itinerant swordsmen.
The living trunks still blossom in the spring. They let water through, but it is never cold.
Boots shaped from consecrated root-wood, still pulsing with the Treefather's vigour. They offer firm footing and resist both thrust and cut slightly better than common elven craft.
Boots forged of a set of steel plates to protect your fragile toes.
Polished gilbranze greaves, layered atop one-another to protect the ankles and feet. The marching, metallic stomps of those who yet walk without lyfe heralds destruction wherever it is heard.
Frayed bronze greaves, shingled atop boots of rotted leather. The toebones of its former legionnaire remain within, rattling about with every step taken.
Plated boots which stir with the same violence driving our world. They have treaded a thousand skulls.
Gilded tombs do worm enfold.
The lone and level sands stretch far away. ‎March forth to the edge of reality, leaving behind its corpse.
The lone and level sands stretch far away. ‎March forth to the edge of reality, leaving behind its corpse.

Antiquated sabatons, fitted to leather boots that've been reinforced with layers of iron maille. While it has largely fallen out of favor with Psydonia's knights since the advent of custom-fitted steel sabatons, it nevertheless remains an excellent choice for those who'd rather not catch an career-ending arrow to the knee.

Resplendant sabatons of pure gold, adorned with angled greaves that proudly bear the holy sigil. Its besilked cuffs have remained surprisingly bereft of debris - not even a sprig of lint remains to be criticized.

Resplendant sabatons of pure gold, adorned with angled greaves that proudly bear the holy sigil. Its besilked cuffs have remained surprisingly bereft of debris - not even a sprig of lint remains to be criticized.

Padded sabatons of bronze, tightly strapped together and padded with hide from a fearsome beaste. The sandals clack about, yet they do not feel obstructive; if anything, you've never felt more agile while beplated.

A pair of leather boots, reinforced with smaller steel plates along the feet and ankles. Woven into the top of each boot's cuff is a thick layer of chainmail, which further protects the wearer's lower legs from harm. A favorite amongst men-at-arms and clerics, alongside the occassional plucky squire that's a few sizes too short to properly wade in them.

A pair of leather boots, reinforced with smaller iron plates along the feet and ankles. A thick layer of chainmail has been woven across the cuffs of each boot, and tastefully riveted into place. Colloquially known as 'soldier's boots', due to its widespread usage amongst Psydonia's oft-conscripted levies.

A pair of leather boots, reinforced with smaller bronze plates along the feet and ankles. A thick layer of chainmail has been woven across the cuffs of each boot, and tastefully stitched into place. Between the glory of Ur-Syon's collapse and the rise of the Celestial Empire, these soles carried the steps of armies-a-plenty across the yet-supple steppes.
Leather sandals, with steel ankle-protectors and socks of sturdy cloth.
The bells add a jostling jingle jangle to each step.
Leather boots lined with fur.
Leather anklets lined with fur for a little extra protection while leaving the feet bare.
Cloth anklets lined with fibers for warmth while leaving the feet bare.
Finely crafted boots, made to stomp out darkness.

description.text: Made to both ENDURE and incite debate within those few Noc-Sainted within Otava. Noc-lit walks, yae or nae? The lenses look like they can be brushed aside with a carefully guided right-pointer finger led motion.

A set of goggles of an older design, made to protect the wearer from sandstorms.
An eyepatch, fitted for the right eye.
An eyepatch, fitted for the left eye.
Half of your face turned gold.
Half of your face turned gold.
Runes and wards, meant for daemons; the gold has somehow rusted in unnatural, impossible agony. The gold is now worthless, but that is not why the Naledi wear them.
A brown sack with eyeholes cut into it.
An ordinary brown sack. This one has eyeholes cut into it, bearing a crude chalk drawing of Psydon's cross upon its visage. Unsettling for most.

It is said that the original version of this mask was used for obscure rituals prior to the fall of the Empire of the Holy Celestia, and now it has been repurposed as a veil for the cunning hand of the Otavan Orthodoxy.
 
Others say it is a piece of heresy, a necessary evil, capable of keeping its user safe from left-handed magicks. You can taste copper whenever you draw breath.

A mask shaped after the snarling beasts of Dendor.
A metal mask adorned with arachnid iconography. A grim visage crafted by a grim race.
Polished gilbranze, molded into an intimidating visage. Touch the cheek; it is warm, like flesh. But it is not flesh. Not yet.
Frayed bronze, molded into an unblinking visage. Only the statues, buried within the innards of Mount Decapitation, share its wrinkled lip and sneer of cold command.
A heavy copper mask that conceals and protects the face, though not very effectively.
Glimmering bronze, curved to veil its wearer's face from both judgement and harm.

Glimmering bronze, meticuliusly shaped to mimic the guise of another. One of civilization's oldest superstitions is the belief that donning such masks would impart a sliver of the mimicked facebearer's power unto its wearer.
Glimmering bronze, curved to veil its wearer's face from both judgement and harm.

Glimmering bronze, meticuliusly shaped to mimic the guise of another. One of civilization's oldest superstitions is the belief that donning such masks would impart a sliver of the mimicked facebearer's power unto its wearer.

A silver mask, forever locked in a rigor of uncontestable joy. The Order of Saint Xylix can't decide on whether it's meant to represent Psydon's 'mirthfulness,' 'theatricality,' or the unpredictable melding of both.
Shattered jaws, chipped teeth, sunken metal - fit for a skull of the same. It snarls in mimicry of the Sinistar's visage.
A steel mask, made for those who have snouts, protecting the eyes, nose and muzzle while obscuring the face.

A steel mask shaped like the face of a rather charismatic fellow! Pronounced cheeks, a nose, and a large mustache. Well, people outside of Aavnr don't think you'd look charismatic at all wearing this.

A steel mask shaped like the face of a rather charismatic beastman! Pronounced cheeks, a nose, and small spikes for whiskers. Well, people outside of Aavnr don't think you'd look charismatic at all wearing this.
A wood mask carved in the visage of demons said to stalk the mountains of Kazengun.
A wood mask carved in the visage of the fox spirits said to ply their tricks in the forests of Kazengun.
"The first lesson of war is that it would be better to live in peace."
"The second lesson: Rich men have dreams. Poor men die to make them come true."
For when one wants to conceal their face while performing dastardly deeds in the name of the crown.
Tiny drops of white dye mark its front, not unlike teeth. A smile that leers from shadow.
What better laboratory than the blood-soaked battlefield?
An important person, warrants the largest beak of them all.
A mask in the shape of a skull, designed to terrify.

Runes and wards, meant for daemons; the gold has somehow rusted in unnatural, impossible agony. The most prominent of these etchings is in the shape of the Naledian psycross. Armored to protect the wearer's face.

A golden mask, gnarled by the sustained agonies of djinnic corruption; yet as long as its Naledian hexes endure, so too will its wearer. Hand-fitted shingles flank the sides to repel incoming strikes. '..Clad with the stereotype of abruptly disappearing without any forewarning, the typical Sojourner is in constant pursuit of diversifying their erudition. One might arrive to learn the local witch's recipe of sanctifying atropa extract and spend yils in the community trying to master it, while another might work alongside the region's Orthodoxic chapter to slay a lycker lord in exchange for his archive, only to vanish the very next day..'
To advance, at any cost.
A strip of cloth tied around the eyes to block vision.
A strip of cloth tied around the eyes. It's too transparent to block vision.
A black cloth mask for those masked duelists, doesn't grant any protection, but covers your eyes, and your identity... somehow.
Keeps the wearer focused ahead. Made of reinforced leather.
You shouldn't be seeing this.
A jade mask that both conceals and protects the face.
A cerulite mask that both conceals and protects the face.
A rosestone mask that both conceals and protects the face.
A shell mask that both conceals and protects the face.
An heartstone mask that both conceals and protects the face.
A amber mask that both conceals and protects the face.
An onyxa mask that both conceals and protects the face.
An opal mask that both conceals and protects the face.
A ceramic mask, forever stuck with the joyful smile its patron god favors. Alt+RMB changes style, Shift+RMB toggles snout form, and Shift+MMB toggles identity concealment.
A rigid pair of protective goggles made for fencing bouts, shielding the eyes without concealing the face.
Steel duelist goggles forged for the most punishing exchanges. They guard the eyes while leaving pride and identity uncovered.
Bronze duelist goggles offering modest protection without obscuring one's features. Every victory deserves a witness.
A padded cloth mask with a visor, it will prevent bad smells more than damage.
A padded leather mask with a visor, it will prevent bad smells and some damage.
A padded chainmaille mask that will protect against some damage and can be rolled down to show your identity.
A padded chainmaille mask that will protect against some damage and can be rolled down to show your identity.
A padded chainmaille mask that will protect against some damage and can be rolled down to show your identity. The fluted design is meant to deflect blows and increase durability.
A padded chainmaille mask that will protect against some damage and can be rolled down to show your identity. The fluted design is meant to deflect blows and increase durability.
Delicate, thin-lensed spectacles of foreign make, their craft finer than most local wares. This variant has a darker tint to its lenses.

Runes and wards, meant for daemons; the gold has somehow rusted in unnatural, impossible agony. The most prominent of these etchings is in the shape of the Naledian psycross. Lightly armored to protect the wearer's face.
You will not conquer. You will endure. In pain, you affirm the Architect's design.
An eyepatch, fitted for the right eye. It has an almost imperceptible gap so that you can see something.
An eyepatch, fitted for the left eye. It has an almost imperceptible gap so that you can see something.
A ceramic mask, forever stuck with the joyful smile its patron god favors. While it will shatter easily from blows, its smug countenance shall taunt its foes.
A remarkably plain veil meant to conceal ones face... if you wore this, a gust of wind would be all it takes to reveal your identity.
Tragedy, neutrality, and comedy; the guise of a master, tempered against the most sorrowful and sudden consequences of bad medicine.
A beaked guise, stuffed with herbs to keep one's humors unmarred during more grizzlesome labors.
A sleek, contoured halfmask of silk.
Death has come to your little town, Sheriff. Now, you can either ignore it, or you can help me to stop it.
An ivory ceramic mask, plain and vacant. What is a joke with a smile missing? Ever so drought of what used to be painted with colors and joy.

An ancient ceramic face. It looks weathered, the sort molded by Xylixian worshippers of many yils past. Even when cast aside, it feels like the hardened clay has never left your hands. As if it always finds a way back into your palms.
Cheap and easy to make. It's better than leaving your neck exposed.
A cheap and simple gambeson coif meant to be worn on its own or under a helmet. It's better than nothing.
A heavier padded coif meant to be worn on its own or under a helmet. Layered properly, it can last through even the busiest of daes.
Sturdy. Durable. Will protect your neck from some good lumbering.
Offers superior coverage to a simple gorget, though it sacrifices some protection in return.

Polished gilbranze rings, linked together to form a billowing hood. Let it not be a crown of thorns that saves this dying world, but a crown of ambition; of fettered metal and stained bone, rejuvenated by Zizo's will to herald Her greatest works yet.

Frayed bronze rings, linked together to form a billowing hood. Shrapnel peppers the linkage; arrowheads and speartips, brought along from a battlefield who's history - and legionnaires - have been lost to tyme.
A thicker and more durable piece of neck protection that also covers the mouth when pulled up.
A coif of meticulously crafted iron rings. It isn't steel, but metal is metal, and it might just save your life.
A maille-hood, fashioned from interlinked bronze rings. As preached by the Pantheon, these maille-hoods were originally made in mimicry of what was worn by the earliest priests.
Offers superior coverage to a simple gorget, though it sacrifices some protection in return.
Offers superior coverage to a simple gorget, though it sacrifices some protection in return.
A series of steel plates designed to protect the neck.
Near them, on the sand, half sunk, a shattered visage lies.
Curled plate, cradling the neck. Once, they were chains - now, they've allowed you to break free.
A series of iron plates designed to protect the neck.

A jutting slab of bronze, traditionally mounted atop a panoplic assembly to veil the neck from precise strikes. To tip the chin up while grounded is an ancient gesture; one which willingly beckons for the 'gift of mercy'.
A series of iron plates designed to protect the neck.
A series of iron plates designed to protect the neck.
A thick garment of steel maille and padding, traditionally attached to bascinets. It's burdensome on the shoulders of those who aren't properly trained to wear knightly garments.
Polished gilbranze plates, layered atop one-another to guard the neck. The spine; a sacred leyline between spirit and sinew. It must remain unsevered, lest Her blessings be lost.
Frayed bronze plates, shingled together to shroud the neck. Primitive scrapes line the flanks, yet the center seems to've been cored out by a spear's thrust.

A series of resplendant golden plates designed to protect the neck, traditionally worn atop a jacket or cuirass. The holy sigil between its buckled halves promises to carry the flame of its wearer, no matter what strike's poised its way.

A series of resplendant golden plates designed to protect the neck, traditionally worn atop a jacket or cuirass. The holy sigil between its buckled halves promises to carry the flame of its wearer, no matter what strike's poised its way.
An interlinked veil of bronze plates, shielding the throat from terrible wounds since the dawn of tyme. Piercing blows may sunder the plate, but - as long as the alloy persists - so shall you.
An antique and simple protection for the neck, used more as an accessory by the common folk. But poor protection is still better than nothing.
Nature knows not of mercy.
A series of interlocking rings of metal set around the throat. Used by the kouken of Kazengun for precisely the same reason as the knights of Psydonia.

A metal collar that seems to radiate an ominous aura. A pale imitation of its artificed counterpart. 
Looks like you'd need someone else's help to take it off.
'With every broken bone, I swore I lived!'
A symbol of ambition from an era that had reason to believe in it.

'Ambition. Destiny. Ascension. A mandate, commanded by God, to be fulfilled by Man. She called us forth from the edge of reality - and with Her dying breath, rasped out the final truth; the fire is gone, and the world will soon follow.'
'Look upon mine works, thee-mighty, and despair!'
An amulet, typically worn by the Holy See's own influential figures. Stalwart for centuries against the darkness. Both a mark of station and grace.
As sure as the sun rises, tomorrow will come.

Similar to a normal amulet of Astrata. This one is blessed and made of silver. A queen does not bargain; she does not relent. Neither shall her followers - least of all the members of her clergy - for with PSYDON gone, Astrata bears the burden of His lineage. All of creation is within her scope, and so too is all of the realm within yours. Stay the course, lest she turn her gaze and everything falls to the scourge of heresy.
There is always more to know, more to learn, more to be.
Knowledge predates lyfe and death itself. Who art thou, to assume the quill's works are no holier than a sword or masterwork?
To fear the unknown is to turn away from the greatest mysteries of all.
If you need something to worship, then worship life. Every last crawling bit of it.
The certainty of death is a reminder to enjoy the time you have.
The healthy wear a crown only the sick can see.
What are you fighting for?
From the ashes, creation.
In a world full of horror and hardship, all we have is each other.
In lyfe a smile is sharper than any blade.
'A man with nothing can still have faith!'

'A comet capable of rending all the enemies of humanity apart; oh, how graceful His power was! And His sacrifice, ever so noble! Yet now He slumbers, unaware of the fruits His efforts came to give. And He sighs. And He weeps.'

'YOU FIGHT WELL, RAVOX OF UR-SYON. YOUR CLEMENCY HATH BEEN EARNED. SURRENDER NOW, AND GRAGGAR SHALL-'‎	'No.' ‎	'-WHAT? YOU'RE GOING TO THROW AWAY YOUR LYFE FOR A GOD THAT HAS NO LOVE FOR YOU?' ‎	'One of us will.'
'We are Her soldiers, the Legion of light.' 'We are the center, the depth of the Sun.' 'Fire and flame - we are one.'
Stone to steel, bone to bronze, mulched to masterworked.
'EVERYTHING - AND EVERYONE YOU LOVE - WILL BE GONE! WHAT WILL YOU HAVE, AFTER THE LAST FIRE'S BEEN SMOTHERED OUT?!' ‎  '..You. I'd still have you.'
'The horrors persist, but so do I!'
A silver psycross beneath a fine layer of gold, honoring Naledian tradition without forsaking the Inquisition's silver. 'Purity afloat, for paradise awaits!'
'Purity afloat, for paradise awaits!'
'It occured to me that our God had left us, but not our ability to endure hardship. We shall make something out of this world, I said, before we pass onto the next.'
'Until my heart ceases beating, and until my vigil ends - I will bring you down with me!'
An amulet made of white pearls, usually worn by fishers or sailors.
An amulet made of rare blue pearls, usually worn by priests and worshippers of Abyssor, or as lucky charms for captains of ships.

A necklace of strung-up sea shells, the calming noise they make when they clack together is reminiscent of a shellfish's claws. They remind you that while men no longer live in water, Abyssor will always remember our origins.
A beaded bracelet made from sea shells, their rough exterior and glossy interior reminding you that Abyssor's children hide the best gifts at the deepest spots beneath the waves.
In moments of quiet it whispers softly, as though deciphering the silence itself.
An amulet with a pristine eye embedded into it. Blind to everything, but to that which shines in gold.

Made out of the silver from the Zybantine mercenaries' first pay. A tradition is kept between these hired blades: to give this one away to someone is to symbolize a debt in their favor - to be redeemed by any other mercenary in times of need.
A beautiful amulet made of solid gold.
An ornate amulet representing a prestigious noble house.
Gold shaped into the form of a skull and strung into an amulet.
A peculiar icon of worship from a foreign land. Forming the three-progned Psydonite cross in a circular ring, this bracelet embodies the Naledian belief of Psydon's eternity.
This is a debug parent item. If you are seeing it meow at the coders.
A sturdy leather collar.
A leather collar with a jingly cowbell attached.
A leather collar with a jingling catbell attached.
A sturdy collar made of leather, commonly worn by field workers.
A specialized collar designed for medical practitioners, with reinforced padding.
A cabbit's foot necklace. Some say it brings good luck. It only feels more lucky when it's worn around the neck.
A massive gemerald, meticulously chiseled into a skull and affixed to a chain. It's mocking me, isn't it?
A familiar necklace, blisteringly hot to the touch. Yet, as warm as it gets, the metal does not sear my flesh. It whispers with divine inspiration; should I dare don it?

'Let His name be naught but forgot'n.' The alloy is familiar, but unmentionable. Blood oozes from cracks within the psicross; ensnared in a perpetual state of half-coagulation. A deathly chill tugs your neck, and your cheeks feel wet - are those tears?
A metal collar that seals around the neck, making it impossible to remove. It seems to be enchanted with some kind of vile magic...
A comfortable and thick collar made of wools and cloth, not protective but it sure keeps your neck warm.

A blacksteel chain, laced through a dozen of the Hoardmaster's golden teeth. Perhaps given as a gift to the wearer, or taken in a fit of mania. It matters not. Those who don this necklace are given a boon from the Hoardmaster, should they be deemed worthy. 
If not, well...
You shouldn't be seeing this.
An amulet carved from jade.
An amulet carved from cerulite.
An amulet carved from onyxa.
An amulet carved from heartstone.
An amulet carved from amber.
An amulet carved from opal.
An amulet carved from rosestone.
An amulet carved from shells.
An amulet carved from beetle chitin.
'Doth thee wish to live deliciously? Mortality is but a shackle; and if you wish to break free from its steely grasp, all you need to do.. is put thine faith in me.'
He was but one flame in the dark. Together, his flock shall outblaze the tyrant sun.
Blood leads only to glory, and violence begets divinity. Nothing less. Conquest is simply another name for victory.
A hollow promise rendered in gold. It weighs heavy with the memory of sweet wine turned to poison, and the comfort of a sorrow that refuses to fade.
The Ten eternal, strength in unity. Stalwart for centuries against the darkness.
Ward of silver, sigil of eternity; by the Ten, I command thee back to Hell!
A thick ruff of trapped fur, worn about the shoulders.
An otavan fashion, a strip of tied cloth that can be donned on the neck to make oneself look more sophisticated.
A ridiculous lace collar typically worn by jesters.
A basic cuirass of iron, protective and moderately durable.
Flexible cowhide armor. Lightweight, better than nothing.
A light armor of wildbeast hide. Far more durable than leather.
A helmet made of leather.

Chain leggings composed of interlinked metal rings.

A knee-length maille skirt, made with hundreds of small bronze rings. It wards cuts against the thighs without slowing the feet.
Interlinked metal rings that drape down all the way to the ankles.

Polished gilbranze rings, linked together with bindings of silk to form a waist's vestment. These undying legionnaires once marched for Vheslyn, and again for Zizo; but now, they are utterly beholden to the whims of their resurrector.
Frayed bronze rings, linked together with bindings of rotting leather to form a waist's drape. The maille jingles with every step, singing the hymn to a cadence once savored by marching legionnaires.
Interlinked bronze rings that drape down all the way to the ankles.
Interlinked metal rings that drape down all the way to the ankles.
Cuisses made of plated steel, offering additional protection against blunt force and projectiles. These are specially fitted for the captain.

a fine webbing made from spidersilk, popular fashion within the underdark
A pair of baggy pants of Ranesheni origin, with a long banner-like cloth draped between the two pant legs.

A pair of cloth leggings, traditionally worn in conjunction with one's shortclothes. These can be combined with maille hosen for the perfect blend of function-and-fashion; just pray no one has the mind to aim below the belt.
Thick hide cut and sewn into a pair of very protective trousers. The dense leather can turn away errant chops.
A thick hide pair of shorts, favored by some for their ease of motion in spite of being less protective than full trousers.
padded leather armor made by Otavan tailors, its quality is remarkable.
A pair of white pants decorated with red stripes and traditional patterning.
A pair of loose breeches with leather reinforcements on the waist and legs. Worn with a cup.
Padded pants for extra comfort and protection, adorned in vibrant colors.
Foreign pants, with leather insewns.
Weird pants typically worn by the destitute in Kazengun. Or, those looking to make a fashion statement.
Tight fitting leather pants worn under clothing of the steppes.
A form of Kazengunite peasant's trousers. The fabric used in their manufacture is strong, and could probably turn away a few blows.
Form-fitting legwear. Almost too form-fitting.
Form-fitting silk tights layered over fine drowsmithed maille.
Good quality trousers worn by laborers.
Good quality trousers worn by laborers.
Good quality trousers worn by laborers.
Form-fitting legwear. Almost too form-fitting.
Dark leather trousers adorned with far too many buckles to be pragmatic.
Heavily padded trousers. They're stained by countless herbs.
Thick leather trousers designed to protect the wearer from sparks or stray gear projectiles. Judging by the scouring, its had plenty of use.
Classy leather tights, form-fitting but tasteful.
A pair of rustic leather poleyns, made to provide basic protection to the kneels.
A formal pair of trousers.
A pair of formal trouser shorts, fit for any strapping young lad.
A handmade pair of baggy, thin leather pants. They end in a tight stocking around the calf, ballooning out around the thigh.
A handmade pair of baggy, thin leather pants. Keeps sand out of your boots, sun off your legs, and a creacher's fangs from piercing your ankles.
Good quality trousers worn by laborers.

Reinforced armor to protect the legs.

Polished gilbranze plates, layered atop silken chausses. Only the few who had embraced undeath were spared from Zizo's ascension; now, they command the undying legionnaires who march forth to sunder creation in Her name.
Frayed bronze plates, shingled over chausses of rotting leather-and-maille. Voided bowels are all that remains of its former legionnaire.
Plate chausses which stir with the innate violence driving our world
But my outside to behold:
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare.
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare.
A set of hanging plates of steel to protect the hips and thighs without too much burden.

short, flowing, and not very modest.

A ring of bronzen resiliance.
Unfortunately, like most magic rings, it must be used sparingly. (Right-click me to activate)

A ring of opulent gold, bearing the symbol of Psydon. By dipping it in melted tallow, it can seal writs of religious importance - a matter better known to the Inquisition, rather than the Church or Crown.
A ring of blessed silver, bearing the Archbishop's symbol. By dipping it in melted tallow, it can seal writs of religious importance.

Born out of duelists desire for theatrics, this ring denotes a proposal — an honorable duel, with stakes set ahigh.

'The hunt, the studying of your prey, the learning of its routes, the knowledge our ancestors passed down, the empowerment of your people and yourself. Learn of the world, or fade away.'		The Plotting Wolf embodies the virtues of progress and knowledge, so that no obstacle nor threat to the homeland remains insurmountable. To understand the truths of beast-and-bronze is to lighten the future's hardships. Do not humor magicka, however, for playing with fire shall always end in someone being burned.

'“The excess of desire, the want of more, the glory of victory, the lover's embrace. Embrace the Leopard, or forget your strength.'		The Relishing Leopard embodies the virtues of love and glory, both in battle and at home. Enjoy the flesh, the drink, and the spice; but be wary to avoid overindulgence, for it shall leave you despondent and lethargic. To become too comfortable is to become weak, and such weakness would turn you into a delicious snack for the Leopard.

'“The hunger, the destruction, the impending frost, the enemy of my enemy. Feed the Bear, or be consumed.'		The Starving Bear embodies not a virtue, but the necessity to thrive above all else. Avarice is not a sin, but a virtue; to ensure that the homeland never suffers from poverty nor starvation again. Pillage, plunder, and perforate the wealth that others would keep from you, but do not forget that every choice begets consequences.

'The battle, the combat, the violence, the rush of victory, the honored glories. Defeat the foe, or die with them.'		The Grinning Moose embodies the virtues of strength and domination; to survive both the homeland's frigid blizzards and those who'd seek to maraud its countrymen. Be untamed and unstoppable, but do not lose yourself in the haze; for even the Moose was chained once. Kill your own without reason, and the chain shall be tugged; and your soul, too, shall be impaled on their horns.

'The world above, of knifetoothed plants and rotting carrion. From jungle to desert, even the stones are nature. Heed its call with the respect it commands, or succumb to madness.'		The Volfskinned Man embodies the virtue of nature and temperance; to live in harmony with the world and its spirits. Pluck a jackberry, plant a seed - Slay a beast, see no part wasted. Yet, temperance must be shown; to take from the world without respect-nor-exchange is to curse the homeland with misfortune. Yet, to completely embrace the world's primality is to lose your humanity - and worse, to become the very beast you hunt.

'The chaos below, of coldblack pressure and crushing weight. Be the current. Control the waves. Reign your sails and hold fast against the storm, or be washed away onto an odyssey with no end.'		The Spiraling Kraken is no virtue, but a presence; the homeland's nautical warden, whose tentacled presence is as unpredictable as the oceans it lords over. To embrace the uncertainty of lyfe is to be rewarded with fortune and mercy when it is most needed. Do not embrace such futility, however, lest you be swept away with all the others into the abyss.
'The memories of the past, and the dreams of the future. A fetish of a beaste, and the carvings of a force that no one beyond your homeland could understand. Sail gracefully, countryman.'

description.text: The finest companion to a javelin and gladius; a deceptively thin-yet-sturdy shield of gilbronze. This alloy even this thin, used to once surpass even steel in durability, yet despite aeon's grip being lifted it will never glitter as it once did.
A near-paradoxally thin-yet-somehow-intact shield of fraying bronze, impossibly remaining barely intact; yet in spite of this, a mere press of the thumb alone will bend a dent into it irreversably.

A heavy venerable shield, far taller and thicker than most other contemporaries, yet masterfully crafted O' so much more as well. Rebuking arrow and bolt alike and yet it serves in a twisted charge against its old purpose to preserve lyfe, serving as a bulwark to herald the march of HER legionnaires to end lyfe.

A tarnished heavy once-venerable shield of fraying, rusted metal. It has survived unspeakable calamities and eons, once rebuking arrow and bolt alike; yet now its no better than a battered hunk of metal with dents threatening to rip open. It failed its former owner and it won't be long until its own frail husk is reduced to nothing.

A series of gears joined around a copper rod. When inserted into a Construct's head, it will allow them to grow their skills beyond their original design.

mechanics.text: Many foodstuffs can be sliced into smaller portions by left-clicking them with a knife on the 'CUT' or 'CHOP' intents. This includes most meats, vegetables, fruits, bread, pies, cakes, saloumi, butter, salo, and more.
Most food will eventually rot, if left out for long enough. Storing food in a closed chest or atop a platter will effectively prevent it from rotting.
Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.
Chopping raw meat on a table with a knife, cleaver, or dagger turns it into mince. Mince can be used for advanced recipes, or used to make 'more out of less' in a stew's broth.

Left-clicking a fire while holding a knife, dagger, or stake in your off-hand allows you to roast raw meat. Roasting meat is quicker than cooking it and can be done without proper cutlery, but has a higher chance of failure.

A bottle with the aurorian brewhouse cork-seal. An Elvish beer brewed from an herbal gruit.
A bottle with a generic leaf cork-seal. An Elvish beer formed by distilling cabbages. You're pretty sure you can make your own with certainly higher quality.
A bottle with the Dwarven Federation Trade Alliance cork-seal. This beer, known as butterhairs: is widely considered one of the greatest exported by the Dwarves.
A bottle with the House Stoutenson cork-seal. Stonebeards Reserve is one of the most legendary beers in existence, with only a few hundred barrels made every year.

A bottle with the House Stoutenson cork-seal. This strange liquid is considered as the most spicy and alcoholic drink in all the Mountainhomes. Bought by nobles of all ages, mostly those with a deathwish.
A bottle with the City of Norwandine cork-seal. It contains a respectably pure, clean voddena.
A bottle that contains a generic red-wine, likely from Zybantium. It has a red-clay cork-seal.
A bottle that contains a Grenzelhoftian classic with a black ink cork-seal.. An extremely sour wine that is watered down with mineral water.
A bottle with the Otavan Merchant Guild cork-seal. This one appears to be labelled as a relatively young red-wine from the coinlord state.
A bottle with the Otavan Merchant Guild cork-seal. This one appears to be labelled as a sweet wine from the colder northern regions.
A bottle gilded with a silver cork-seal. It appears to be labelled as an elvish red wine from Otava. Likely worth more than what an entire village makes!
A bottle gilded with a golden cork-seal. This is the legendary Valmora Blue from the Vineyard of Valmora, headed by a sainted Dark-Elf swordsmaster. This bottle would swoon Gods over!
A regal-looking bottle with an avantyne cork-seal. Faint whispers of somebody's darkest secrets can be heard coming from the bottle.
A bottle with a Saigabuck cork-seal. This dark liquid is the strongest alcohol coming out of Grenzelhoft available. A herbal schnapps, sure to burn out any disease.
A bottle with the Apfelweinheim cork-seal. A cider from the Grenzelhoftian town of Apfelweinheim. Well received for its addition of pear, alongside crisp apples.
A bottle with the Rockhill-crest cork-seal. An especially tart cider from the duchy of Rockhill. Myths say the brewers let the barrels age in the bog, which results in that especially strong flavour.
A bottle with the City of Norwandine cork-seal. A red ale brewed to perfection in the lands of Hammerhold.
A bottle with a Shieldmaiden Berewrey cork-seal. A deep red honey-wine, refined with the red berries native to Gronns highlands.
A bottle with a simple cork-seal. A golden honey-wine brewed in the Avar Steppes. Manages to keep a proper taste while staying strong.
A bottle with a simple cork-seal. A murky, white wine made from rice grown in the steppes of Avar.
A bottle with a Running Saiga cork-seal. A form of alcohol brewed from the milk of a saiga and salt. Common drink of the nomads living in the steppe.
A bottle with a Yamaguchi Brewery cork-seal. A pale lager brewed in the far-away lands of Kazengun, refined with green tea for an unique flavour-profile. Even lighter than elven-brew!
A bottle with a Golden Swan cork-seal. A translucient, pale-blue liquid made from rice. A favourite drink of the warlords and nobles of Kazengun.
A bottle with a Golden Swan cork-seal. A reddish-golden alcohol made from a fruit commonly found on the Kazengun-isles. A favourite of the commoners.
A bottle with a Golden Swan cork-seal. A clean alcohol made by distilling rice. With a dry and clean finish. Popular amongst the warrior caste of Kazengun.
A bottle with a red seal. A strong, sweet yellow rice wine that is often used in cooking.
A bottle with a red seal. A strong, clear liquor made from fermented sorghum or rice. The favored drink of wandering warriors.
A bottle with a red seal. A strong, sweet rice wine infused with medicinal herbs, including Ginseng. Often prescribed as a medicine on the Zhongese mainland.
A bottle with a red seal. A strong rice wine with a dead snake inside. In the land of Zhong, It is believed that drinking this will improve one's virility and blood circulation.
A bottle with a Possumtail Brewery mark. A special brew made from murky water and swampweed. A Heartfelt special.
A bottle with a blue, Crescent moon mark. A special brew that is extremely potent and toxic, but strengthen the body. If you dare.
A strange bottle with a concerningly brown color. It bears the seal of a snake's head over a leaf. Markings indicate the contents are supposed to be good for health...
A dusty, ancient bottle with a red-ochre coloring. It bears an intricately detailed golden skull seal, and the markings on it are clearly of the Shogunate. It looks to be filled with herbs inside.
A clay bottle that contains a generic red-wine, likely from Zybantium. It has a red-clay cork-seal.

A scroll imbued with an enchantment of unyielding light. Causes an enchanted item to glow with light.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of storage. Doubles the storage space of a container.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of revealing. Doubles the range of lightsources.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of darkvision. Good for seeing in the dark.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of unbreakingt. Causes an enchanted item to be able to take more punishment..
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of featherstep. Makes you speedier, and makes your footfalls silent.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of fire resistance. Prevents you from catching fire.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of spider-climbing. Helps you clamber up difficult surfaces.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of thievery. Helps you steal and pick locks.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of longstriding. Provides easy movement through swamps.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of smithing. Provides more effective hammer strikes on anvils.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of lyfe stealing. Heals you occasionally when you hit a living foe.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of lightning. This enchantment shocks foes with a chance to spread to nearby friends and foes alike.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of voidtouched. This enchantment pulls foes briefly into the void, and spits them out nearby.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of frostveil. Slows enemies that hit you when applied on armor, or enemies that you hit when applied on weapons.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of phoenixguard. Sets those that strike you on fire.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of wound closure. Allows you to periodically seal wounds.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of returning weapon. Enables you to summon an existing weapon back to you.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of sharpshooting. Provides the wearer with better ranged weapon skills.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of infernalflame. Hitting an opponent sets them on fire.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of freezing. Freezes your foe in a block of ice when struck.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of temporal. Teleports you back to where you were hit, a few seconds after being hit.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of briar's curse. A weapon with this enchantment does more damage, but damages its wielder in return.
A scroll imbued with an enchantment of chaos. A weapon with this enchantment causes random effects.
The white hot flame of a mage's light on a mage blue background, these banners mark the colleges and laboratories of the Mage's Guild.
The white hot flame of a mage's light on a black background, these banners mark the colleges and laboratories of the Mage's Guild.
A wall of pure arcyne force.
A wall of pure arcyne force.
An immensely strong wall of pure arcyne force.
An immensely strong wall of pure arcyne force.
arcyne door
arcyne door
arcyne door
This fountain produces a strange blue liquid. It seems faintly magical. Attempts to bottle it seems to cause it to inexplicably turn into water.
This forge uses cycling magma from an internal core to heat things.
A curious arrangement of stones.
A smooth unnatural Obelisk, looking at it provides the sense of unease.
Strange symbols pulse upon the ground...
subtype used for arcane rituals- you should not be seeing this.

arcane symbols litter the ground- is that a wall of some sort?
A massive sigil- is that a wall in the center?
A large spiraling sigil that seems to thrum with power.
A relatively basic confinement matrix used to hold small things when summoned.
An adept confinement matrix improved with the addition of a sealate matrix; used to hold things when summoned.
An thoroughly warded confinement matrix improved with the addition of a sealate matrix; used to hold larger, dangerous things when summoned.

name: noc's eye warded sealate confinement matrix

description.text: An thoroughly warded confinement matrix improved with a Noc's eye sealing measure and the addition of a sealate matrix; used to hold the largest, most dangerous things summonable.

A clump of dirty lustrous nuggets!
A gleaming ore of moonlight hue.
A dark ore of rugged strength.
A burnished ore with reddish gleams.
A mass of soft, almost malleable white ore.
Dark lumps that become smoldering embers later in life.
Wood that has been burnt and transformed into charcoal. Can be used to fuel fires or used to smelt iron.
Red gems that contain the essence of quicksilver.
Solid wealth in your hands.
Forged strength. Essential for crafting.
This bar causes a gentle tingling sensation when touched.
An ingot of strangely soft and malleable essence.
A hard and durable alloy favored by engineers and followers of Ravox alike.
This bar radiates purity. Treasured by the realms.
This ingot is a stalwart defender of the realm.
Sacrificing the holy elements of silver for raw strength, this strange and powerful ingot's origin carries dark rumors..
This bar radiates a divine purity. The Psycross and the words casted into the surface denotes the Otavan Inquisition as the point of it's origin.
A decrepit slab of wrought bronze, uncomfortably cold to the touch. The gales shift into whispers, when held for long enough; 'ambition commands sacrifice'.
A timeless alloy of gold and bronze, hence the name gilbranze. The reflection on its surface isn't yours; it smiles back at you with eternal malice.
Solid wealth in your hand- Hey, wait a minute, this isn't gold!
A mass of wrought bronze, rendered lame from the forge's heat. Sometimes, dead is better.

A slab of metal, aged and bare. You finally know what it is, yet no word can be sired to describe it. '..none will ever know the greatest truths; of Aeon's grasp, of Adonai's presence, of Psydon's fate..' '..but, perhaps, that's for the better. The malaise is gone, but the evils of this world are still very real..' '..find a way to give the remains a new lyfe; a new vessel that may yet make the Archdevil weep..'

A slab of obsidian, crackling with energy. Your fingers blister from the sheer heat, radiating off of its glassy surface. '..no man, be-they a saint or sinner, can truly withstand such power..' '..but, perhaps, you are different..' '..find a way to give the remains a new lyfe; a new vessel that may yet make the Archdevil weep..'
Something that you were likely never meant to see. Pray to a higher presence for assistance, before rendering it asunder in the forge's flames once more.
Fractal violence, gleaming with a crimson haze that beckons for its final purpose to be accomplished.
A massive hunk, born from the incoherent fusion of molten iron. Chunks of ore-and-ingotry peak out from its jagged surface, yearning to be refined - be it into ingots, or something more purposeful.
A massive blade, forged from a raw heap of iron. The unique spike-styled tang seems to be longer than what'd be seen on most greatswords, stowable only by the innards of a fittingly large handle.
A massive handle, assembled from the double-handed grip of an Executioner's Sword. The unique crescent-styled crossguard seems to have a slot, fittable only by the tang of a fittingly large blade.
This tool is essential to mine in the dark depths.
With a reinforced handle and sturdy shaft, this is a superior tool for delving in the darkness.
A so-called 'legionnaire's tool'; antiquated, but nevertheless beloved by many for its versatility. It offers an answer for labors both above-and-below, courtesy of its bronze axhead-and-picktip.
you shouldn't be seeing this, scream at a coder!

A long handled dolabra axe-pick with a carved grip made of hardened maple wood. This one has an axe-blade of frayed blacksteel, having lost its varnish long ago with a long pick-head behind the blade, this dolabra is decorated with golden reinforced bracers along the shaft and a heavy gold mace head at the top.
A long-handled dolabra axe-pick with a carved grip made of hardened maple wood. Fitted with an axe-blade of polished blacksteel and a long pick-head behind the blade.
a long handled dolabra axe-pick with a long shaft of treated oak. Fitted with an axe-head made of polished albranze with a fitted pick-head behind the blade.
Glimmering with silvered blackness, this is a pretigious tool for miners delving into the darkness. It looks like it will strike hard enough to shatter any boulders within a rocky surface instantly.
Stone versus sharp stone, who wins?
A chisel of wrought bronze, which once labored to gather the ores necessary for an ancient alloy; such was lost in the aftermath of Her ascension.
A copper pick, slightly better than a stone pick.
A station to give your apparel a fresh new color! Recommended to use with white items for best results.
A sizeable brush made of the finest mane-hairs. Thick dye adheres to it well.
A wooden frame with taut threads ready to weave fabric.
A rack for drying meats or scraping hides into leather. It can be moved with the help of a wooden stake.
Stores and withdraws currency for accounts managed by the Grand Duchy of the realm.
A Crown which craves the brow of miesters and the vault's jawbank; it could be also be mounted upon a restrained person's head to drain their miester account in a pinch.

mechanics.text: Strike it with coin to pay for what you buy. Whatever isn't spent comes back as CHANGE.
Its owner can UNLOCK it with its key, or a keyring holding it, to restock it and withdraw the profits.

description.text: Never gets tired, does not ask questions, only minor signs of tampering. Alas, fashioned with copper of low quality.
Created by a fanatical sect of devout followers of Ravox, this machine sets bounties.
A weathered scroll enchanted to list the active bounties from the Excidium.
A chair-shaped machine normally used to place cursed collars onto a prisoner's neck. This one's been tampered with, and now does the opposite - re-purposed to remove those wretched iron collars.
A chair-shaped machine normally used to place cursed collars onto a prisoner's neck. This one's clearly been tampered with, and looks suspicious.
A chair-shaped machine that collects bounties, for a greater reward, in exchange for a penalty that some might consider worse than death.
these eerie trinkets dangle from awnings, etched into the shape of a leering face. Hung above protected areas, to give interlopers a forboding sense of Being Watched...
these eerie trinkets dangle from awnings, etched into the shape of a leering face. Hung above protected areas, to give interlopers a forboding sense of Being Watched...

The crier's most trusted friend.
You want to destroy your life.
A brass-plated contraption with a coin slot above and an iron strongbox beneath. The guild posts and fulfills smithing or engineering work here, coin held in escrow until the job is done.

mechanics.text: Any commissioner may build a manifest of smithing or engineering recipes and deposit coin into the machine. Submitting the manifest posts an order with the coin held in escrow.

A smith can claim an open order, deliver the finished items back into the machine, and collect the escrowed pay once every item has been delivered. An order that has been claimed cannot be cancelled by the commissioner.
Unlocked with the guildmaster's key, material prices and margins can be adjusted.

description.text: A brass-plated commission board for the weavers' and tailors' guild. Coin held in escrow until the work is delivered.

mechanics.text: Any commissioner may build a manifest of smithing or engineering recipes and deposit coin into the machine. Submitting the manifest posts an order with the coin held in escrow.

A smith can claim an open order, deliver the finished items back into the machine, and collect the escrowed pay once every item has been delivered. An order that has been claimed cannot be cancelled by the commissioner.
Unlocked with the guildmaster's key, material prices and margins can be adjusted.
This commissioner accepts tailoring and garment work only.

description.text: A machine that indulges in humenity's oldest profession; killing. The heads of Dendor's creechers, goblins, and brigands go in, and the bounty is credited directly to the bearer's account - less the Crown's Headeater Levy, of course.
A fleshy, immoving golem with a nasty grin. You can clearly tell it isn't alive, yet the scent of its putrid flesh is strangely alluring.
A little, putrid fleshy nodule that can be further shaped into various fleshy items.
A sickly-sweet scented rose. Like honeyed rotten meat. It's dim petals seem laced with a black ooze that retreats away from your fingers.

A pestran invader of Abyssor's divine sea. These are well known to latch onto the corpses of underwater leviathans. More than a pest, leechticks suck the soul out of those that disturb them, digesting the lux of assailants.
This leechtick has feasted on lux and digested it. A crazy person might use this for revival...
An empty canister yearning to be filled with chimeric heartbeast blood.
A canister full of viscous blood, despite being closed it somehow still exudes a putrid smell. Highly valued, due to their ability to purify lux.
An empty vial yearning to be filled with chimeric heartbeast blood.
A vial full of viscous blood, despite being closed it somehow still exudes a putrid smell. Highly valued, due to their ability to purify lux.
What? Ewww!

A specialized holder designed to securely hold chimeric aspect canisters. The crystal reinforces the creature's personality, increases it's thinking capacity. The brighter the red glow of the crystal, the better the aspects match the creature.
Formerly a covetous creature, this one now shares its Hoard with the Freefolk. Protecting the transactor's Hoard, and trading it for Favor.
A large shirt with heavy padding meant to be used below armor. Will probably stop an arrow, unlikely to stop a bolt.
An infinite, yawning hole that makes or breaks men. Come and play!
Carrier zads have fallen severely out of fashion ever since the advent of this hydropneumatic mail system. A coin slot activates the mechanism for dispensing parchment(a zenny) and quills(a ziliqua).

A ferocious little beast that hoards a mountain of goods under its home. The dreaded creechur is willing to part waes with its lower quality items..for a price.
Sweet, sweet, addiction. Love in the veins, comfort in my heart.

A machine that attracts the attention of trading balloons.

mechanics.text: Drop items on the tiles around the navigator. Trading balloons arrive periodically and lift the goods away, leaving mammon in change on this tile.

description.text: Freedom has a price.

mechanics.text: Drop items on the tiles around the navigator. Trading balloons arrive periodically and lift the goods away, leaving mammon in change on this tile.

description.text: A navigator kept under the Merchant's own roof.

mechanics.text: Drop items on the tiles around the navigator. Trading balloons arrive periodically and lift the goods away, leaving mammon in change on this tile.

description.text: A wide crate stamped with the seal of the Ferentian Trading Company. Goods deposited here are accepted against the demands of foreign vessels in port - the depositor is paid in mammon to their account, less the Crown's export duty and the Merchant's middleman cut.

mechanics.text: Left-click with an item to deposit it for matching ship demands. You must have a NERVELOCK account to deposit - the crate will refuse goods otherwise.
Right-click to dump everything on your tile into the crate at once.
Certain items like kegs can be click dragged or offloaded in hand.
Stacks, handcarts, and bins are unloaded automatically.

description.text: A cabinet of sealed correspondence and official records, recording the accomplishments of the Ministers of yore. A councillor bearing an agreed charter may be sworn in here. What's more, a Ministry's signet ring could be re-issued here with ten zenarii.
They may hold money for you.
A large wooden notice board, carrying postings from all across Rotwood Vale. A ZAD perch sits atop it.
A large wooden notice board, carrying postings from all across Rotwood Vale. A ZAD perch sits atop it.

A rosewood board scented with bath-oils, hung with perfumed slips of parchment. The bathhouse's workers pin their offerings here for any passerby to peruse.
The stomach of this thing can been stuffed with fluids for you to buy.

Its owner can UNLOCK it with its key, or a keyring holding it, to restock it and withdraw the profits.
Strike it with a container to put it in the slot. Drag a tank's level, or use + and -, to draw from as many tanks as you like, then POUR. Prices are per dram.
It sells empty bottles and vials from separate shelves. One bought goes straight into the slot, so take your own container out first.
While it's UNLOCKED, pour the slotted container into a tank, flush a tank onto the floor, or set a tank's label and price. Empty bottles and vials struck into it go on their shelves.
While it's UNLOCKED, right-click with a bag to empty its filled containers into the loading tank and shelve its empty bottles and vials.
If it breaks, its tanks spill across the floor.

description.text: A massive ledger book with gilded edges, sitting atop a pedestal with the Mercenary's Guild banner. Its myriad enchanted pages are filled with various contracts and bounties issued by Mercenary's Guild, with arcane scripts that appears and fades as contracts are issued and completed.

mechanics.text: Left click to open the Grand Contract Ledger, where you can sign new contracts and abandon ones you hold.
To turn in a completed contract, click the ledger while holding the quest scroll.
Retrieval-quest items should be dropped onto the marked tile in front of the ledger.
Abandoning a contract forfeits its deposit to the treasury and places you under a brief guild cooldown before you may abandon another.
Heads taken from contract targets carry no bounty - the contract's reward is payment in full. Beasts and brigands you hunt outside a contract still fetch coin at a HEADEATER.
The Innkeeper may compose rumor contracts here, spending Rumor Points to seed retrieval, courier, and light kill jobs across the realm.
Your fellowship may turn in contracts you hold on your behalf, should you fall in battle. The reward and levy is credited to the one who turns it in, using their tax exempt status, if any.

description.text: A sturdy piece of paper used to wrap items for secure delivery. The final size of the parcel depends on the size of its contents.
A sturdy piece of paper used to wrap items for secure delivery. The final size of the parcel depends on the size of its contents.

A writ calling for a blockade to be cleared blockadeThe bearer is enjoined to travel to the blockaded region and break three successive waves of raiders - each wave must fall within fifteen minutes, and the Steward may recall the writ should the bearer takes too long before  before reaching the blockade. Hand this writ over to a person] and they may initiate the contract; pin it to the Grand Contract Ledger and it will demand a Fellowship of three before it can be taken. Every additional person at the blockade, until the sixth, will attracts more enemies and rewards. If brigands are sitting on stolen Crown coins, breaking the blockade will seizes the hoard and have it taxed by the Crown as Recovered Spoils.

A contract issued by a member of the town.Hand it to an adventurer and they may take it up regardless of fellowship requirements. Pin it to the Grand Contract Ledger and it waits for whomeever will sign

A scroll oft known as a "whispering scroll". Enchanted to whisper the target's location to its bearer while they yet live, and to mark itself silently upon their death - so the bearer need bring no head, no hand, no token of proof beyond the writ itself.
The magical protections make it resistant to damage and tampering. It will only whisper when carried on the person of the contract bearer.
Something is closing in...
An artificed flagpole. It responds to distant signals to show which of the town's important figures are currently active...
Used to signify your presence in town. Middle click to set a custom notice on the flagpoles in town, use to raise your flag or lower it.

Also known as the People's Mouth, so long as the people can afford the ratfeed to pay for it.
The Loudmouth's own gleaming horn, its surface engraved with the ducal crest.
A guest's horn. Not as gaudy as the Loudmouth's own, but still a fine piece of craftsmanship.
Also known as the People's Mouth, so long as the people can afford the ratfeed to pay for it.
An iron and gold choker with an emerald gem.
An ever-attentive ear...
A faded coin with a ruby laid into its center.

The order of Saint Malum was tasked with coming up with a way for the Orthodoxy to communicate with each other, while still being able to seal missives with tallow. After three yils of restless toil, they came up with this marvel of otavan technology. May your communications endure.
 There is a button on the side. It urges you to press it.

The Supernatural Communication Optical Machine is a wonder of magic and technology, able to transmit and receive messages across long distance. There's a button in the MIDDLE for making private jabberline connections.

The Receiving Communication Optical Machine is a much cheaper, ubiquitous version of the SCOM, designed only to receive message over long distance. They are oft found outside of the town, especially in older ruins.

A heavy ring made of metal. There is a gem embedded in the center - dim, but alive.
A rusty shoddily-made metal ring. The gem embedded within is barely holding on.
A lavish golden ring with the mark of the Crown. Heavy and garish. The gem embedded flickering in excitement.
A basic metal ring. It has a well-cut, dismal gem embedded - bearing the mark of the Crown.
Sweet secrets whispered so freely.
A brass-trimmed contraption with a hopper above and an iron strongbox beneath. Bring rag-and-bone and broken stock; the scrapper weighs the offer and pays in coin. The proprietor sets the rate.

mechanics.text: The proprietor lists per-material prices, capacities, and which wares to call out. Coins fed into the machine fund the coffer; when it runs dry, the scrapper turns away offers.
Strike with an item to offer it. The scrapper weighs by what it would smelt down to.

description.text: A brass-trimmed contraption with a hopper above and an iron strongbox beneath. Takes whatever a smith can smelt back into ingots.

mechanics.text: The proprietor lists per-material prices, capacities, and which wares to call out. Coins fed into the machine fund the coffer; when it runs dry, the scrapper turns away offers.
Strike with an item to offer it. The scrapper weighs by what it would smelt down to.

description.text: A brass-trimmed contraption with a hopper above and an iron strongbox beneath. Takes whatever a tailor can rework into fabrics.

Strike with an item to offer it. The scrapper weighs by what it would smelt down to.

description.text: The stewards most trusted friend.
A crisply-stamped sheet summarising yesternight's dispatches to the Nerve Master. Meant for the Steward's eyes on rising.
A machine near where Crown-hired clerks tally exports. Wares left within reach of this machine are counted toward Crown standing orders.
A magitech device connected to the trade network. Users can buy basic goods, crafting materials, and food for a price from these units, or sell them here for money.

mechanics.text: Left-click with an open hand to check the vomitorium's stockpile. Stored mammons can be used to purchase a wide variety of materials, which're then vended out for use.
Left-clicking the machine with an item will load it into the stockpile, rewarding you coinage in turn. Make sure to register an account with the NERVELOCK, first, or you won't receive any coinage.
Right-clicking the machine will automatically load all adjacent items into the stockpile at once.
The vomitorium's stockpile naturally refills over time. Loaded items are added to the stockpile's quantities, which can then be vended by others or exported by the Steward for profit.

description.text: Xylix determines if we shall be granted freedom, or ignored for eternity.
This machine controls the punishment for victims of the salt mines.
Only ticket winners may get to ride the sorrid slide to freedom. Looks like it will strip whoever passes through.
A big throne, to hold the Lord's giant personality. Say 'secrets of the throat' with the crown on your head if you are confused.
He who wears the crown holds the key to this strange thing. If all else fails, demand the "secrets of the throat!"

A kin of the HEADEATER, its brass gullet re-tuned by the Bathhouse for gentler appetites. Feed it any trinket and the prize is whisked away to the Nightmistress's vault - where the hoard remembers its worth. Its jaws open only for the Bathhouse's own.
Collects and secures the treasury of the Grand Duchy of the realm.
A biomechanical obelisk that holds the alms and tithe of the Church's faithful. Throttle it with a strike to spill that which is rightfully yours.
A biomechanical obelisk that secures the coffers of the Ferentian Trading Company. Throttle it with a strike to spill that which is rightfully yours.
A biomechanical obelisk that secures the takings of the Bathhouse. Throttle it with a strike to spill that which is rightfully yours.
A biomechanical obelisk that hoards the tavern's takings. Throttle it with a strike to spill that which is rightfully yours.
The stomach of this thing can been stuffed with fun things for you to buy.

mechanics.text: Strike it with coin to pay for what you buy. Whatever isn't spent comes back as CHANGE.
Its owner can UNLOCK it with its key, or a keyring holding it, to restock it and withdraw the profits.
Left-click with an open hand to browse its wares. Several of one ware can be bought at once.
While it's UNLOCKED, strike it with an item to stock it. Right-click with a bag to load what's inside, or with an open hand to load everything on the floor in front of it.
Wares of the same kind and name are sold together at one price. Renaming wares to match another's name merges them at that ware's price.

description.text: Give this thing money, and you will immediately buy a neat property in the capital.
