description.text: A magitech wall device connected to the local trade network. Users can buy basic goods, crafting materials, and food for a price from these units, either from in-town or imported for a heftier price.

mechanics.text: Left-click with an open hand to open the vomitorium. Insert mammons to fund purchases, then buy or import goods from the local stockpile.
Withdrawals are cheapest. Direct imports pay a surcharge - duty flows to the Crown once Royal Custom is invoked.
The vomitorium does not buy goods. Take deposits to a stockpile instead.

description.text: A small cage made to ride on a belt. Empty perches inside. Too awkward to fit in most containers.
A great coop of wood and iron where carrier zads are kept, fed, and dispatched abroad.
A zadcote of the stewardry, kept open to any members of the Royal Court.

A Ferentian Trading Company zadcote. The brass plate reads FTC and a tally of late dispatches. The zads are sold exclusively by the Ferentian Trading Company (officially), and sourced from the zad training grounds in Rosporth, where elven and humen keepers raise zads and train them to navigate and home in. In the yil 1421, in the nascent yils of the Company during the Actions off Rosporth between the Ferentian and Etruscan Trading Company, the Ferentian company attempted to use its newly acquired zads to bombard the Etruscan ships. Unfortunately, most of the zads homed back onto the FTC ships, leading to the loss of at least four warships and a hundred men. Since then, FTC has limited the usage of bomb zads to within Ferentian territories.
A bathhouse zadcote. The perches are warm with steam, a faint smell of incense in the air.

A highly-practiced reading of the body's humors and hidden ailments performed afar with left-handed magicks. Reveals a target's condition, with greater skill in medicine granting deeper detail. By embedding a Forceps on your patient, you may even identify substances within the blood; but even the most unskilled physicker can tell from a Cheele or Leech's reactions.
Examine a structure's details through invoking Enochian magicka to see the world through Zizo's design without the need of specialised tools, close or afar.
Drains the targets stamina, unless they worship Abyssor. Also makes them dizzy and blurs their screen.
Throws target down if they are on water, otherwise puts them off balance.
Rise if fallen, and regain some of your stamina.
Compel a fish to leap out from targeted water tile and towards you.
Heals target over time, more if there is water around you. Weakens if cast away from water for too long
Calls a Mossback that is friendly to you and that you can command.
Summons a Dreamfiend to hound your target.
Consumes an anglerfish to bless target with ability to call upon Abyssal Strength.
Buffs all your stats besides fortune, and lowers your perception.
Ignite a flammable object at range.
Focus Astratas energy though a stationary psycross, reviving the target from death.
Removes the limit on your vision, letting you see behind you for a time, lasts longer during the dae and gives a perception bonus to those skilled and holy arts.
Ignite a target in holy flames, burning those that surround them. Fire burns brighter within devout Astratans.
An ancient miracle, honed by those who'd served as Astrata's martial arm in the second era. With such, you may beseech Astrata for a mote of Her power.
A spear of light, pulled from Her domain. Throw far. Strike true.

Bless a targeted soil plot or tree. Druidic Trickery increases stored charges. Revives dead plants, gives them nutrition and water if low & boosts their growth. Blessed seed powder can expend all charges to bless up to five nearby planted soils at once.
Pacifies a targeted tameable beast with Dendor's blessing, permanently soothing its anger. Has 2 charges; each restores in 10 seconds, or 1 minute if both are spent.
Summons glowing mushrooms that shock people that try moving into them. Dendorites are immune.
Summon vines nearby.
Draw upon the the secrets of the hidden firmament to converse with the mooncursed.
Makes spiders not attack the target.
Channel Dendor's most sacred blessing to consecrate a living, unburnt tree into a sanctified tree of the Treefather — a nexus of druidic power.
Call forth a lesser dryad from the grove to serve as your guardian. Cast again to send it back.
Activate, then middle-click a turf or creature to command your lesser dryad to surge there with thorns and vines.
Command your lesser dryad. Cast and click yourself to follow, a tile to guard there, or an enemy to attack.
Conjure a flower or bush seed into your hand using Dendor's power. Seeds dissolve if dropped. Flower seeds can be changed in-hand to subtypes. 30 second cooldown.
A bed of flower petals that looks soft enough to sleep on! Said to spare the dying from Necra's domain.

Summon a sacred Eoran bed to provide sanctuary and stabilize the wounded. You may only maintain a limited amount of beds at a time depending on miracle skill. Summoning a new one will cause the oldest one to vanish.
An ominous violet fluid that seems to pulse with faint light. It's made out of strange shimmering glass. Looks fragile.
A flower of gentle petals, associated with Eora or Necra. Usually adorned as a headress or laid at graves as a symbol of love or peace.
Tries to grow an Eoran bud on the target tile or on the targets head, forcing their thoughts away from violence until removed.
Makes the target both high and drunk.
Forge a symbiotic bond between two souls.
Bless a food item. Items that take longer to eat heal slower. Skilled clergy can bless food more often. Finer food heals more. Eoran masters can make food a golden hue.
Grow a pomegranate tree that, when tended to, grows Aurils with a variety of effects. Additionally heals beautiful people and HEAVILY debuffs both STR and PER for everyone in visible range.
A mystical tree blessed by Eora.
A mystical pomegranate glowing with inner light. It feels warm to the touch.
A glowing seed from the fruit of Eora. It pulses with divine energy.
A blood-red seed that seems to pulse with vitality.
A pink seed that radiates beauty and grace.
An iridescent seed that shifts colors in the light.
A deep blue seed that smells of the ocean.
A geometrically perfect seed that hurts to look at.
A golden seed that radiates warmth and life.
A grey seed that feels glacial to the touch. An IMMENSE sense of dread can be felt just looking at it.
A blood-red seed that seems to pulse menacingly.
A blindingly bright seed that radiates pure life energy. It imitates lux, the essence of life.
A milky-white seed that pulses with purifying energy.
A silky soft seed from Eora's sacred tree. It can be used to propagate her gift in fertile soil.
Bestow a person with Eora's calm, if only for a little while.

Heals target over time, causes damage if something is embedded in target. Burns undead instead of healing them if you worship the Ten.
Does not work on those worshipping the dead god.

Improves the targets ability to receive healing, buffing all healing done on them by 50%
Burns undead instead of healing them if you worship the Ten.
Heals all wounds on a targeted limb.
Transfers the blood from myself to the target with divine magycks. Ratio of transfer scales with holy skill.
Restores the targets Energy, Twice as effective on someone else.
Damages Armor, Forces target to drop a metallic weapon, heats up an ingot in tongs or smelts a single item.
Damages structures in an area while possibly knocking down mobs in the area.
Melt a pile of valuables and convert them into a single item. Sacrifice is accepted even if its not valuable enough to make anything.
Ignites target.
Consecrate a coffin or a grave. Sending any spirits within to Necras realm.
Stuns and explodes undead.

Opens a one-way portal into a realm on the edge of death, People can be dragged into the portal to prevent their decay. Undead with be set aflame. Those whom enter the domain will find their Will to continue heavily weaken. 
Necras domain can be left through a portal within to a shrine, or a grave/psycross marked with necra's sight.
Call upon the Undermaiden to let your words reach a departed soul, and hear their whisper in return.
Call upon the Undermaiden to guide you to a lost soul.
Direct a mote of living darkness to temporarily blind another, restricting their combative skills relative to your faith.
Direct a mote of living darkness to temporarily blind another. This imperfect replica of divine magick requires a Naledian Psycross to function.
Make another (or yourself) invisible for some time. Duration scales with the arcyne skill. Casting, attacking or being attacked will cancel the duration.
Make another (or yourself) invisible for some time. Duration scales with the holy skill. Casting, attacking or being attacked will cancel the duration.
Allows you to learn a spell or two of a certain type once every cycle.
Peer ahead.
Shutter voices and empty the air of sound - naught mage-nor-man shall utter a word, be it invocation or insult.
Wrap a target in a ward of anti-magic.
Reshape flesh through divine craft.
A foul, tarry black substance. It seems to writhe with unnatural energy.
Examine another's vitals.
Examine another's vitals.
Attach all limbs and organs you or your target is holding, and near your target.
Causes a swarm of bugs to surround your target, bites them and causes sickness. Infecting targets gives you charges to use other spells.
Invoke Pestras will though a Psycross to cast out rot from people or regrow their flesh.
Burn out the rot by Astratas will.
Manifest leeches inside of target, causing them to puke them out while restoring some blood and curing minor poisoning.
A greater heal, more effective on targets affected by some form of greater rot. Requires infestation charges to cast.
A miraculous heal that can restore even the most grievous wounds, including missing limbs. But it requires being at maximum infestation capacity. No force can resist this miracle.
Enchant your blade with Pestra's power, consuming one infestation charge to make your next strike against an infested target more potent. Negligible effect if the target isn't infested...
Bless your next strike to do extra damage and slow the target.
Grants you and all allies nearby a buff to their strength, willpower, and constitution.
Harms Undead and encourages the livings wounds to close faster.
Casts out a chain that tries to pull the target closer.
Bring an opponent with you to Ravoxian Trial. Engage in 3 minute combat.
Where the challenger will return after the trial is decided.
Where the challenged will return after the trial is decided.

Revive the target at a cost, cast on yourself to check.
a dreamfiend will stalk the target and sap their stats until confronted by them.
Summon the dreamfiend haunting you to confront it directly
Revive the target by consuming heartblood. Self cast for more information.

Revive the target at a cost, cast on yourself to check.
The target will get hungry faster for a time.
Revives the target? Grants them a random debuff from other revivals, small change to be worse or better.

Revive the target at a cost, cast on yourself to check.
Targets willpower and strength will be sapped for a time.

Revive the target at a cost, cast on yourself to check.
Targets strength and speed will be sapped for a time.

Revive the target at a cost, cast on yourself to check.
Requires a wise tree or sanctified tree nearby. Targets speed and constitution will be sapped for a time.

Revive the target at a cost, cast on yourself to check.
Targets intelligence will be sapped for a time, in addition they will be burned by moonlight.
Spins the wheel, either buffing or debuffing the targets fortune.
Throw one's voice into a object
Creates a body double of yourself and makes you invisible, after a delay your clone explodes into smoke.
Mock your target, reducing their INT, SPD, STR and WIL for a time.
Jumps you up to 3 tiles away.
Disappear in a flash of smoke! (With a range of 4 tiles)
Play a sound of your choice at the targeted location, or assume the form of an item as a parlor trick, you brilliant jester.
Challenge your luck and your patron
Turn a leech into a Abyssoid using your own blood.
Transform a normal tree into a wise tree of Dendor.
Summon an inhumen blade.
This blade throbs, translucent and iridiscent, dark energy ready to aid me in combat...
Say something funny to someone in high spirits, it will brighten their mood.
Remind someone in low spirits that it could be much worse.
Chill the target with necrotic energy. Severely reduces speed and weakens physical prowess.
Raises an undead guard in your servitude.
Raises a formation of simple minded undead skeletons. Inferior shamblers. Husks in everything but zeal.
Raises a formation of simple minded undead skeletons. Inferior shamblers. Husks in everything but zeal.
Conjure an evil, devilish skeleton from the death realms of Bite. Maximum of two, don't be greedy!
Raises a simple minded undead skeleton. Inferior shamblers. Husks in everything but zeal.

Oftentymes, husks and shamblers walk aimlessly - uncertain of their future. Befriends the undead Requires the target to be within four tiles. Works on undead animals, too, and they will heed your command.
Adds or removes a target from the list of allies exempt from your undead's aggression.
Commands skeletons. Cast on turf to head in that direction ignoring all else. Cast on self to command it to follow, cast on target to attack them, Cast on a lesser skeleton to set to idle-aggressive,
Bleed for the target, taking their wounds and refilling their blood level.
At the cost of some lyfe sustaining blood, I can stand still to focus on mending my injuries.
Stand still to focus on mending your injuries. You shall PERSIST.
Absolve the target, taking their damage as your own, potentially even shouldering their death at the cost of your Lyfe.
A lesser form of the mighty art of ABSOLUTION, bereft of its means to revive. Transfers the wounds from your target to you. Use carefully.
You siphon a portion of your blood, in exchange for empowering your next strike. Those struck will find their actions tiring and cumbersome. A greater miracle.
At the cost of your own lyfe giving blood, you can inspire your fellow Psydonites. Such grants them constitution and willpower. A greater miracle.
In exchange for your flesh, you may replenish your lyfe giving blood. A greater miracle.
In exchange for your flesh and lyfe giving blood, you are protected from Her puppets. Any undead striking you are harmed in turn. A greater miracle.

A miracle of an ancient order, allowing one to form portions of their lux into suitable implements. In your case, projectiles, for your beloved sauterelle. The effects of such are only felt shortly after use, so be swift. A greater miracle.
A bolt, formed of pure, unfettered lux. Your own, likely, if you're holding this. Surely you can understand what's meant to be done?

mechanics.text: Projectiles have maximum and minimum falloff ranges, with particular falloff factors for damage.
If the target is hit between the maximum and minimum tile range, then the full force is delivered.

description.text: An unholy rite to claim hearts as a tribute to Graggar. Only works on fresh corpses.
Spin a translucent web on your current location.
Spin a thick, opaque web on your current location.
Call your saddled drider companion to your side. Usable outdoors or in the Underdark.
Send your drider away while outdoors or in the Underdark.
Call your drider to your side. Unlike those wretched surface mounts, the noble drider is unbothered by trivialities like hostile terrain or fauna; an apex in its own right.
High Five?
Accelerate your allies with your bardic song!
Play a dirge which inflicts misfortune upon thy foes. -2 LUCK to non-audience members nearby.
Play a dissonant dirge that slows your enemies. Reduces SPD of non-audience members nearby.
Inspire the rhythm of battle, your allies strike and parry 20% better!
With cat like tread, apply light steps to audience members
A song for thinkers, +3 INT
Play a dirge inspired by Pestra. Leaving the droning of insects in their ears! (-1 WIL -2 CON non-audience members)
Recuperate your allies spirit's with your song! Refills stamina over time!
Recuperate your allies bodies with your song! Refills health slowly over time!
A steadying melody that bolsters your allies' constitution.

Attune your weapon to a rhythm. Your next melee hit within 8 seconds triggers its effect. An instrument is required in your off hand, though highly talented bards can make do with their voice, so long as they are able to be heard.
Prime a parry-bypassing strike for 20 brute damage to your aimed location. Armor still applies.
Prime a strike that repels the target by 1 tile.
Prime a strike that heals you for 0.5 per tick for 10 seconds.
Prime a strike that leaves the target sluggish for a short time.
Prime your next melee strike to unleash a 3x3 blast based on your last rhythm. Build 3 rhythm procs to unlock.
GETTING HURT MAKES YOU ANGRY, MAKE THEM HURT BACK- MORE HURT IS MORE ANGRY!
A circle of arcyne power woven into the land.
A hammer of pure arcyne force.
An arcyne tether anchored to the leyline. Destroy it to sever the connection.
This blade throbs, translucent and iridiscent, blueish arcyne energies running through its semi-transparent surface...

Shoot out a blast of divine power! Deals more damage to heretics(Psydonians/Inhumen) and Undead! 
Damage is increased by 100% versus simple-minded creechurs.
Can be fired in an arc over an ally's head with a mage's staff, spellbook or psicross on arc intent. It will deals 25% less damage that way.

Channel unholy power and sunder the unbelievers. Deals additional damage to wretched conformists and Psydonites! 
Damage is increased by 100% versus simple-minded creechurs.
Can be fired in an arc over an ally's head with a mage's staff, spellbook or psicross on arc intent. It will deals 25% less damage that way.
Let out a piercing celestial call that disrupts all veils of shadow within sight.
Mark this location with a name, binding it to your hidden trail.
Vanish and reappear at a hidden trail you've marked before.
Shrouds nearby allies in illusionary invisibility, broken if they move or act.

Uses Origin Magick to gradually rewind a target's body to a healthier state. The effects happen in order, and only one at a time. Removes embedded objects, stops bleeding, grants health regeneration and energy recovery. The nature of time-based manipulation allows this to work on most targets.
Converges the targets past and present, empowering your Naledi arts to last longer.
You capture your target's current state in time, reverting them to such a state several seconds later. If under Convergence  when expiring, your target will keep any healing they receive.
Displace a target slightly ahead of local time, dramatically increasing their speed and reactions. When reality catches up, the resulting temporal strain leaves them sluggish and exhausted.

Shatters a target across several competing timelines, briefly immobilizing them and spawning 4 to 8 Time Echoes around them. Recovering an echo restores the target's vitality, while destroying one forces reality to violently reconcile the contradiction, inflicting damage.
A discarded possibility struggling to remain real.
Heats the air around you.

Watch the fire dance and join the dance together! 
The ground under your feet will burn!
I Yell out, driving away forest animals, this is from my experience living on these lands and hunting so long. This won't work on more intelligent creatures
check for good ore
dig for clay on some dirt or mud
Examine a structure's details

Fit Clothing will allow you to fit a cloth or leather garment to an individual, allowing greater durability for a time 
You can increase this time with an essence of wilderness, seeping it into the material
\
Take on an individual as your protegé, allowing them to level up their weapon skills past Expert. This ability gains a charge with the passing of each dae.
Massage a client, working out the soreness in their muscles

Help another refocus their studies. Sacrifice a skill level in a skill above Journeyman to gain 3 sleep advancement points and a 30 minutes buff that will increase intelligence by +2 but reduce willpower by 1.

You can take on an apprentice, giving them a trait and Novice in corresponding skills. You can only have one apprentice and you cannot take someone who already have a mentor as your apprentice. 
Should your apprentice disappears completely (e.g. leaving the round), you may take on another apprentice.

You can teach a skill or language to another person, provided they are not more skilled than you in it. 
You cannot teach the same person twice. Teaching takes 30 seconds, and requires both you and your student to be focused on the lesson.
Explode in a wonderful blast of osseous shrapnel.
Explode in a wonderful blast of osseous shrapnel.

Raise a single greater skeleton that serves you. They are imbued with a fragment of a soul and is more intelligent than usual, simple-minded lesser undead.
Should the spell fails to find a suitable soul, a mindless undead will be summoned in its place with decrepit equipment.
This will only happen if you are in combat mode, to avoid any accident.
Take on the form of one of Dendor's sacred beasts.
A comprehensive reference tome cataloguing all known arcyne disciplines, aspects, and utility spells. Its pages shimmer faintly with residual magic.

Said to house the essence of the condemned Wizard 'Mineester the Omnipotent', whomst was punished for his hubris and arrogance. His grand punishment is to serve as a simple tool for answering any and all the questions that may be posed by all the Magos of Psydonia. (CLICK WITH THE ORB TO ANSWER YOUR QUESTION)
A shimmering wall of arcyne force. Projectiles cannot pass through from the front.
An arcyne ward placed by another mage. It cannot be dismissed - it must be weathered or destroyed.
A rare hunk of arcyne energy projected in front of the caster. Slower and more deliberate movement by blades and melee weapons easily pierce through to the squishy Magi behind.
An invisible barrier of arcyne energy protecting the wearer.
An arcyne ward hardened with draconic scales. Resistant to flame.
An arcyne ward crystallized with leyline energy. Tough against blunt force but less rigid than plate. Shatters violently when broken.
An art mastered by Naledi Sojourners. A barrier against the winds of fate, powered by their own spark. Magyks will have no effect upon the user.

An argument between the chosen of Noc and the Otavan Orthodoxy has raged on for years.
No-one truly knows who the original creator of these glasses was.
But one thing, at least, is certain: they are quite fashionable.
Death has come to your little town, Sheriff. Now, you can either ignore it, or you can help me to stop it.
A wall of pure arcyne force.
A magical piece of paper that has been transcribed upon.
A mystical parchment that records spoken words when activated, and can transcribe them when deactivated.
Get out of the way!
A cloud of freezing mist that chills to the bone.
Freezing mist blankets the area.
A slab of conjured ice
A slick glaze of ice.
A whirling maelstrom of spectral blades!
A khopesh of condensed arcyne energy, conjured from raw mana by a Ferramancer's will.
A rapier of condensed arcyne energy, conjured from raw mana by a Ferramancer's will.
A greatsword of condensed arcyne energy, conjured from raw mana by a Ferramancer's will.
A twin-headed greataxe of condensed arcyne energy, conjured from raw mana by a Ferramancer's will.
A halberd of condensed arcyne energy, conjured from raw mana by a Ferramancer's will.
Get out of the way!
A grand maul of condensed arcyne force, conjured from raw mana by a Ferramancer's will.
A wall of conjured stone. It will crumble in time.
A pillar of conjured stone. Sturdy, but not indestructible. Shatters into gravel when destroyed.
Force open adjacent doors, windows and most containers.
Get out of the way!
Conjure forth a wave of energy, repelling anyone around you.
Summons forth dangerous rapid lightning strikes.
ZAPP!!
Freeze your enemy with an icy blast that does low damage, but reduces the target's Speed for a considerable length of time.

Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

Most food will eventually rot, if left out for long enough. Storing food in a closed chest or atop a platter will effectively prevent it from rotting.
Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

Most food will eventually rot, if left out for long enough. Storing food in a closed chest or atop a platter will effectively prevent it from rotting.
Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

mechanics.text: Freshwater can be collected by leaving out buckets, pots, washbins, and any other uncovered containers on an uncovered tile while it's raining.
Pots can be placed atop a hearth by left-clicking it. If the hearth is lit, the placed pot will eventually come to a boil - so long as it's filled with water.
Right-clicking a hearthbound pot allows you to fan its flames, further reducing the time it'll take to start boiling.
Once boiling, left-clicking the hearthbound pot with an ingredient will drop it inside. The larger a pot is, the more ingredients can be dropped in at any given time.
After the first ingredient is placed in, the pot will begin turning it - and any other subsequent ingredients - into a brew, over the course of a minute.
Specific ingredients can create specific brews; dried rosa petals for a refreshing tea, coffee beans for a revitalizing drink, and more..

Once boiling, left-clicking the hearthbound pot with an ingredient will drop it inside. The larger a pot is, the more ingredients can be dropped in at any given time.
After the first ingredient is placed in, the pot will begin turning it - and any other subsequent ingredients - into a brew, over the course of a minute.
Specific ingredients can create specific brews; dried rosa petals for a refreshing tea, coffee beans for a revitalizing drink, and more..

description.text: Crushed rosa petals with humor-balancing properties, yearing to be further dried to draw out its flavor.
Dried rosa petals, fit for brewing a delicious tea with humor-balancing properties. Combining it with some pumpkin spice should help to elevate its fragrance even more.
A palmful of smells so delightfully rich, destined to be distilled into a damn fine cup of humor-balancing tea.
Freshly extracted coffee beans, with a hard texture. Should be roasted first.
Roasted coffee beans, with a much deeper flavor. Can be used to brew coffee. The variant grown in these lands can be brewed without being ground.
Roasted coffee beans, nestled atop a bed of fragrant pumpkin spice. It looks perfect for brewing a particularly rich kettle of coffee.
Dried tea leaves. Edible. Seeds can be extracted from them. Needs to be processed in a millstone.
Ground tea leaves that can be used to brew tea, or further combined with pumpkin spice.
A blend of coarsely-ground tea leaves and pumpkin spice, perfect for brewing the most relaxing drinks in all of Psydonia.
A spiced sliver of heaven, awaiting to be brewed into a velvetly rich drink.
Delicious fattiness, fit for elevating meals-a-plenty.
A portion of milky paradise. Kneading it into dough is necessary to prepare many of Psydonia's pastries, though the more humble-hearted prefer to simply doll up a slice of toast with it.
Clotted and salted milk, eager to be cocooned in cloth so that it may realize its fullest potential. You'll need three more servings of fresh cheese to finish it.

mechanics.text: Many foodstuffs can be sliced into smaller portions by left-clicking them with a knife on the 'CUT' or 'CHOP' intents. This includes most meats, vegetables, fruits, bread, pies, cakes, saloumi, butter, salo, and more.
Most food will eventually rot, if left out for long enough. Storing food in a closed chest or atop a platter will effectively prevent it from rotting.
Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

description.text: Jackberries that've been pruned of their juiciness, and turned into flavorful nuggets. Like the humble hardtack, so too will these raisins outlast their creators.  When combined with honey and doused in a pot of boiling fat, it can birth 'sweetglass'; a shatteringly sweet candy, popular amongst the elders and children-of-nobility.

mechanics.text: Many foodstuffs can be sliced into smaller portions by left-clicking them with a knife on the 'CUT' or 'CHOP' intents. This includes most meats, vegetables, fruits, bread, pies, cakes, saloumi, butter, salo, and more.
Most food will eventually rot, if left out for long enough. Storing food in a closed chest or atop a platter will effectively prevent it from rotting.
Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

description.text: A lump of animal fat, fit for oiling and sausage-stuffing.
Fatty tissue is harvested from slain creachurs and rendered of its membraneous sinew to produce a hard shelf-stable grease.

mechanics.text: Mixing tallow with a filled glass of wine can make 'redtallow', a crimson-tinged wax that's popular for sealing folded letters of ducal- and religious importance.
Mixing tallow with ground tea leaves can make 'greentallow', a sickly green wax that's popular for sealing folded letters of mercantile- and bureaucratic importance.
For more grizzly alternatives, one can substitute the wine with blood, or - in the hands of a trained Inquisitorial agent - a filled INDEXER.

A melding of dried meat, berries, and tallow that has fueled Psydonia's expeditioneers for centuries. It is denser - and arguably less appetizing - than most foodstuffs, but consequently unrivaled in terms of sheer nutritional mirth. Traditionally sliced and dropped into boiling water, in order to make a quick-yet-robust broth.

description.text: Thick, salted biscuits and thicker, saltier slabs of pork fat, and a sprinkling of pepper; a match made in paradise. A spicier but heartier variant of the brothbrique, its portions can be further divvied up with a knife and stewed into a remarkably hearty broth.

description.text: An unbelievably decadant slab of fudge, made with Amazonia's cocoa beans and Grenzelhoft's saiga milk. A recent trade agreement between the two nations has turned this once-expensive delicacy into a slightly-less-expensive treat for many. Following a rather unfortunate diplomatic incident involving a Lupian nobleman and a box of chocolates, chocolate is also now-known to double as a potent 'humor rebalancer' for some of Dendor's children. It looks like it can be split in half with a dagger.

An unbelievably decadant halve of fudge, made with Amazonia's cocoa beans and Grenzelhoft's saiga milk. A recent trade agreement between the two nations has turned this once-expensive delicacy into a slightly-less-expensive treat for many. Following a rather unfortunate diplomatic incident involving a Lupian nobleman and a box of chocolates, chocolate is also now-known to double as a potent 'humor rebalancer' for some of Dendor's children. When combined with pumpkin spice and tossed into a kettle, it makes for an absolutely divine drink.
An ingot of jammified blackberries, fit only for the finest slices of bread. It beckons to be sliced with proper cutlery.
A portion of jammy paradise, bearing the same hues as Ferentia's morning skies. It yearns to be savored not by its lonesome, but upon a slice of bread - ideally, butterdoughed or toasted.

A portion of jammy paradise, bearing the same hues as Ferentia's evening seas. It yearns to be savored not by its lonesome, but upon a slice of bread - ideally, butterdoughed or toasted.
Glassy droppings of tallow-fried sugar, oft-divvied out amongst the youth by Psydonia's wisest and kindliest elders.

Glassy droppings of tallow-fried rocknuts, coated in sugary shells and laced with herbal medicine. Such giblets are popular amongst Psydonia's youth - both as a reward to Otavan children for remembering their scripture, and as a remedy to childhood ailments.

A thick, undulating appendage of dark-furred base tapering into reddish serpentine scales, tipped with a maw-like orifice ringed by interlocking bonelike plates. Even severed, the feelers inside still twitch.

We've been fighting this war against the Zizites for decades. It's been over 60 years by now. 
It's exhausting. Though, after the efforts from Kingsfield and from the Zybantine sands, we've managed to create something beyond the lead spheres of the past. This turns any deadite to gore, and any skeleton's bones to dust.
 No matter how hard their Avantyne is.

A box meant to dispense BRUTALITY towards Zizites, also known as BRUTAL rounds, or Zizite Killers.
When that crazy Dwarf from Kingsfield invented this kind of projectile that surpassed the lead sphere, the entire war on Zizo changed.
The Zizites barely adapted the blackpowder to their undead troops, but we adapted and overcame them.
I still remember when I first put this old tattered thing on. It has been with me for about fifteen yils now. Back then, it was slightly too big for me, but now it fits me just right.
Once the Engineers of the Guild of Craft finally figured out how to make cheap, easily made armor in their autosmithy, this became the norm for most of us.

The Otavans were ingenious, they've had their own masks for decades, and only recently allow us 'peasants' to have the schematics. When the Zizites started using Zizo Bane Gas Belchers and other nasty things, these were issued as standard equipment to everyone. 
These masks are normally fitted with some steel plates for extra protection.

Originally, this was given to us by Pestran Plague-monks a few yils ago. A blessing for the 'marksmen', it helped us deal with the stench of decay, though, over time, the mask lost its actual functionality.
I'm used to the smell of death, anyway.

description.text:
I once sat in a trench for over two daes. In the same spot, overlooking the same area. The only things that kept me alive were my copiettes, and this nifty thing.
Though, it didn't stop the rous bites.

description.text: Although they're uncomfortable, I've grown to like my boots. Tight, but not too tight, they loosen up after standing in mud for weeks on end.
A hardened leather hood reinforced for heat and abuse. It fully encloses the head and face, making its wearer look more like a demon than a man.

description.text: A studded leather coat made for a battlefield pyromaniac; hard-wearing, practical, and built to survive sparks and struggle.
A roaring, clinging flame.
A glob of violently burning material.
You should not be seeing this.
A heavy sealed container, with some arcyne sigils, sealing away incredibly hot lava.
Created in the Great Jade Empire, this Xinyi piece of arcyne wonder is now MY TOY. Such wondrous carnage I shall sow!
Whenever crates of this stuff came around, we knew we'd have to start digging into our own wounds that following dae. Doubles as a small satchel, too.
Also known as the Soldier's Drink, it's commonly used by the Grenzelhoft Military in long expeditions. How did it end up here, though?
A jagged piece of violently propelled metal.
A Grenzelhoftian marvel. It was invented to replace the impact grenade most would know in this time, this is a lot more deadly.
A large, expeditionary backpack often used by Kingsfield forces to carry enough supplies to keep a soldier alive away from friendly lines for a while.

I can still remember when this weapon was given to us. We were fighting on the borders of Grenzelhoft with the Otavans, and this beauty came in a shipment alongside others, and some ammo.
We were...stunned at how effective it was. It killed deadites in a singular shot to the head, and tore through lyfeblood armor like it was hot butter. It wouldn't take long for it to be made a war-crime to use it on your fellow man.
 KZ-41 - it stood for an obvious name.
KILL ZIZITES.
you shouldn't be seeing this i don't think.
Made in bulk in Kingsfield, filling, and surprisingly tasty. It's made from everyone's favorite Eoran blessed Meat Stew.

mechanics.text: Many foodstuffs can be sliced into smaller portions by left-clicking them with a knife on the 'CUT' or 'CHOP' intents. This includes most meats, vegetables, fruits, bread, pies, cakes, saloumi, butter, salo, and more.
Most food will eventually rot, if left out for long enough. Storing food in a closed chest or atop a platter will effectively prevent it from rotting.
Rarer foods and drinks, or those made from more expensive recipes, can provide increased bonuses to the indulger's mood and health.
Everyone has a favorite meal and drink to indulge in - and, conversely, a hated meal and drink that they absolutely despise. Serve them right, and their mood will greatly improve.
Those of nobility have much higher standards, when it comes to what - and how - they eat. They prefer to eat plattered meals with proper utensils, while disliking plainer and cheaper food.
Set a recipe on accident? middleclick the item to reset the recipe back to nothing and pick a different one.

description.text: An empty military ration can. There's still meat stew at the bottom. It looks like something out of Kingsfield!

I still remember when we replaced these over the old SCOMRING. We'd be able to receive orders from so far away. They're powered by arcyne magick, and this one in particular has a piece of the comet in it. They told me it's so they can communicate across 'time'.

You can sense the power of the Comet SYON within this...It must have a very small fragment of it.
A strap for carrying grenades. A lunatic's invention, surely.
A blend of wax, pigment, and oil meant to be applied to the lips.
A blend of wax, pigment, and oil meant to be applied to the lips.

A rapier of sporting a steel blade and decrotive silver-plating. Elaborately designed in classic intricate yet functional Etrucian style, the pummel appears to be embedded with a cut emerald with a family crest engraved in the fine leather grip of the handle.

An imported Grenzelhoftian panzerstecher, a superbly crafted implement devoid of armory marks- merely bearing a maker's mark and the Zenitstadt seal. This one has a grip of walnut wood, and a pale saffira set within the crossguard. The ricasso is engraved with Ravoxian scripture.
A silky smooth emerald-green dress, only for the finest of ladies.
A vest often worn by those of the Grenzelhoftian mages college.
A handcrafted harp.
A gilded steel great axe, a long-handled axe with a single blade made for ruining someone's day beyond any measure..
A gorgeous black and gold dress. It seems the padding was removed.

People bring the small flames of their wishes together... to keep them from burning out, we cast our own flames into the biggest fire we can find. But you know... I didn't bring a flame with me. As for me, maybe I just wandered up to the campfire to warm myself a little...
Two blades, one forged in Noc's light, a soothing breath of clarity. Here, and here alone, were moon and fire ever together.
Two blades, the other born of Astrata's ire, a raging flame of passion. Here, and here alone, were fates severed and torn.
A recreation of a gilbranze greatsword, wrought in steel. Inscribed on the blade is a declaration: "I HAVE ONLY A SHORT TYME TO LYVE, BUT I AM NOT AFRAID TO DIE."
Promises hurt, but so does plucking rosa. Hoping hurts, but so does looking at the beauty of Astrata's light. Pick yourself back up. Remember your promise, despite the thorns.

A fine cloak made from the feathers of Necra's servants, each gifted to a favoured child of the Lady of Veils. While it offers no physical protection, perhaps it ensures that the Undermaiden's gaze is never far from its wearer...

A Blacksteel wrought wooden staff granted to the Mages whomst have graduated from the Celestial Academy, with a shining Dorpel at its head that reminds the caster; There is nothing that cannot be solved with time & innovation.
A small, palm-fitting bound scroll - a writ of commendation for a mercenary of the Realm.
A medal commemorating a job "well" done.

A parody of the brass medal issued to Grenzelhoftian soldiers of great honor and renown. Frequently adopted as medals by other, younger guilds among the mercenaries of PSYDONIA, with slight adjustment.
A pouch, sealed tight, bearing the acorn of an oak native to the vale. May your end be a new beginning for the Realm.
A beautiful silver necklace with pea-sized rontz inlays. Each is a work of art in itself; handcrafted by a master jeweler of Etrusca. This is the blade to which the condottiero has sworn their lyfe.

A luxuriant golden chain worn about the shoulders or neck, a sign of high honor in distant Zybantium. Some claim these are a testament to the origins of the Desert Riders in distant slave-fighting pits, but others think them marks of favor from the highest echelons of the Empire. The desert riders confirm neither rumour.

A trinket bearing the snarling visage of a volf and bolt, a mark of distinction among the Forlorn Hope. Often taken from the dead and issued anew to the living, each bearing lyfetymes of nicks and scratches.

A descendant of the oft-forgotten psilen, with a hole through one end for hanging on a string. With the advent of mammon as the Western Continent's currency of choice, they find new lyfe worn as marks of skill by freifechters.

A humble token of tightly-wound canvas, fur, and wood. A piece of home, clutched tight against the chest. Feel its heart beat in tyme with your own. Even here, in this distant realm, the gods walk, and they walk with you.
"Fergive? FERGET? PFAH! GO T'HEL!"
The underdwellers claim this will always point you exactly where you need to go. If it doesn't work, that's just an issue of skill and mindset.
A medal commemorating a job "well" done.

A fragment of blessed Otavan steel, carefully wrought into an unusual halo-pattern. While it won't do any good against verevolfs or demons, it will remind a distant routier of what they're fighting for: home, blessed Otava, and their Weeping God, PSYDON.

A tightly sealed vial of dirt. These are taken from the land of the Steppesman's Kozak, and given to them as they leave by their closest Kin. When their service ends, if they should see its end, the vial may be emptied, and the glass crushed; the end, it says.

A beautiful gold-and-rontz ring, a masterwork of Etruscan jeweling. This does more than prove you a true vaquero; it shows you are as beautiful as you are dangerous, a crimson stone set against gold. Lyve dangerously, but lyve all the same.

'Carve Naledi as the wind does always - whisper to one white stone, and the others will remember where to stand,' so said PSYDON. 
Within the splitting arms of the psycross, a marble-white shard is embedded within aurum. A fracture of the Great City Naledi which fell; a memory of a thousand wailing generations in their fading, dying breaths as a reminder for who you are.

The husk of a desiccated beespider larva, passed down within the ranks of those whose names have been struck from dark elven history. The old tyranny's uprooting would be their last act of true valor.
An old, decaying scroll of some sort. Marked with odd stains and liable to tear if you're too rough.
A puzzle box.
Corrugated tinplate concealing tinfood.
A daring blend of alchemy, aberrant blood, and divine silver. This panacea fortifies the anointed's body with blessed silverdust, protecting them from the curses of vampyrism and lycanthropy.

A daring blend of trace amounts of purifying lux, aberrant blood, and divine silver. This panacea fortifies the anointed's body with blessed silverdust, protecting them from the curses of vampyrism and lycanthropy.
A letter from the Grand Cathedral in Otava. It reeks of zig smoke.
This pouch holds the ouch.
A box for all your smoking needs.
Simple white chalk. A useful tool for rites.
A Holy Rune of Astrata. Warmth irradiates from the rune.
A Holy Rune of Noc. Moonlight shines upon thee.
A Holy Rune of Xylix. The air feels untrustworthy.
A Holy Rune of Ravox. A blade to protect the weak with.
A Holy Rune of Pestra. A sickle to cleanse the weeds, and bring forth life.
A Holy Rune of Dendor. Becoming one with nature is to connect with ones true instinct.
A Holy Rune of Malum. A hammer and heat, to fix any imperfections with.
A Holy Rune of Abyssor. You sense your mind getting pulled into the drawn spiral.
A Holy Rune of Abyssor. This one seems different to the rest. Something observes.

A pulsating crystal shard that hums with otherworldly energy.
A pulsating crystal shard that hums with the power of the deep. It feels wet to the touch.
A violently pulsating rune emitting storm energy.

A massive crystalline structure pulsing with abyssal energy. Dark ice spreads from its base.
A massive crystalline structure pulsing with abyssal energy. Dark ice spreads from its base.
A massive crystalline structure pulsing with abyssal energy. Salt water spreads from its base.
A Holy Rune of Necra. Quiet acceptance stirs within you.
Eerie glowing thread, cometh from the grave

Proof of ten souls being sent to Necra, formed of a material that is not metal, constantly weeping a minute amount of blood. Ten souls for one, the Ferryman may send one back before Necra fully has them.
A Holy Rune of Eora. A gentle warmth and joy spreads across your soul.
A Holy Rune of ZIZO. Ambition at any cost.
A Holy Rune of Matthios. All has a price.
A Holy Rune of Graggar. Fate broken once, His gift is true freedom for all.
A Holy Rune of Baotha. Relief for the broken hearted.
A Holy Rune of Psydon. It depicts His holy symbol, yet nothing stirs within you.
A slingable sheath made of leather, meant to host surprises in smaller sizes.
A well maintained strap connected to a lacquered wood scabbard with a metal finish. It appears designed to hold an exceptionally long blade.
The natural evolution to the advent of longblades.

A sword's noble scabbard, enamored with elaborate silver decorations. It carries an aristocrat's sword upon a silver platter, and - just like an actual platter - can suffice at riposting an errant blow.
A sword's royal scabbard, enamored with exquisite golden decorations. It pampers a champion's sword in a veil of gilded silk, reluctant to let go.
A decorated cane bearing the visage of a vulture.

Sleek, fashionable and deadly. Traits shared by both staff and the one holding it. Never let yourself be outdone, never rely on merely one trick.The rontz embedded in the handle serves as focus for arcyne arts.
A dagger's noble sheath, enamored with elaborate silver decorations. Oft-flaunted upon the faulds of a knight, it dangles and sways whenever its steely reserve is drawn.
A dagger's royal sheath, enamored with exquisite golden decorations. The hand that draws will spell the fate of many; be it for the kingdom or the world.
A piece of steel lined with wood. Great for batting away blows.
A simple wooden scabbard, trimmed with bronze. Unlike its steel cousins, this one cannot parry.
A simple wooden scabbard, trimmed with bronze. Unlike its steel cousins, this one cannot parry.
A cloud-patterned scabbard with a cloth sash. Used for blocking.
An ornate, wooden scabbard with a sash. Great for parrying.
A plain lacquered scabbard with simple steel hardware. A plain dark cloth serves to hang it from a belt.
A simple lacquered sheath, for shorter eastern-styled blades.
Made to hold everything a people-butcher will need. Contains a list of implements... what even IS a Sisrat?

A strange axe, who knows where it came from. It is searing hot to the blade, the hilt is barely able to be held.

A cute bottle that can hold three swigs of liquid, which is useful for both miserly business practices and preventing accidental overdosing. This one lacks a cork.
A squishy pale gland, filled to the brim with venom of the deadly Aragn spider. Feels cold to the touch.
An ominous vial, filled with venom of the deadly Aragn spider. Feels hot to the touch.
Cast on turf to head in that direction ignoring all else. Cast on a minion to set to aggressive, cast on self to passive and follow, cast on target to focus them. Does not work on greater skeletons.

The basic precept of holy magic orients around the power of prayer and soliciting a Divine Patron for a tiny sliver of Their might.

The fundamental teachings of theology return to you:
 Fill: Beseech your Divine to create a small quantity of water in a container that you touch for some devotion.
 Touch: Direct a sliver of divine thaumaturgy into your being, causing your voice to become LOUD when you next speak. Known to sometimes scare the rats inside the SCOMlines. Can be used on light sources at range, and it will cause them flicker.
 Use: Issue a prayer for illumination, causing you or another living creature to begin glowing with light for five minutes - this stacks each time you cast it, with no upper limit. Using thaumaturgy on a person will remove this blessing from them, and MMB on your praying hand will remove any light blessings from yourself.
 Shove: Lay hands upon an adjacent creature to channel divine restorative power through your touch. Both you and your target must remain still for the channeling to continue.
Shield your fellow man from the Undermaiden's gaze, preventing them from slipping into death for as long as your faith and fatigue may muster.
Debuffs targeted undead as long as they remain near you, slowly getting set on fire if they stay.
Make a vow to Necra. You can never be revived, and only your own limbs can be restored. You will harm undeath and slowly heal, but the healing stops while you lie in crit.
Mark a psycross or a grave marker, and peer through them.
Summon rancorous crows to tear at an opponent!
Gets the target drunk and stops them from overdosing for a time.
Blows dust of a potent painkilling drug at the target, potentially causing overdoses with repeated use.
Numbs the target's pain and improves their mood.
Attempts to discern the target's vices. Depending on the target and your Miracles skill, some vices could be incorrect.

A toast to passion that ends in ash.
 Beseech Baotha to pour wine onto a container. Poisons the unfaithful, rewards Her blessed with healing.
A gift for those whom you have chosen as worthy of Her grace, to be able to imbibe in Her gifts as you do.
Once a flower of love, now touched by Baotha's hand. Its petals whisper of desire, despair, and the kind of longing that never dies. Worn by those who cannot let go.
A frenzy for two to partake in.
Pleasure's perfume, just before the fall.
Revives the target by afflicting them with a lasting addiction.
Grants you and all allies nearby a buff to their strength, willpower, and constitution.
Unleash a terrifying warcry that weakens nearby enemies' will. Those who dodge while afraid are knocked to the ground.
Grants temporary health regeneration at the cost of strength, will, and devotion.
Twist the viscera in your hand into a writhing, unholy net. Cast again to unmake it back into gore. Throw it to snare a foe's legs.
A writhing snare woven from blood and guts. It won't hold its shape for long outside a caster's grip. Throw it, or it'll collapse back into what it was.
The blood of your enemy shall boil, their skin feeling as if it's being ripped apart! Graggar demands their blood must FLOW!!!
Fills you with an adrenaline rush for a short while.

You cannot dominate the dead. Place a pair of EYES upon a fallen mortal, granting them thechance to fight again... for a price. Their intelligence will be drained for some time, or untilthey slay an orcish challenger from His realm.
A jagged tear in reality smelling of blood.
Challenge the rift-born to clear your blood-debt. Must be cast on a nearby floor. Make sure to kill all foes, Graggar will not tolerate further acts of mercy.

Unleash your true rage for two minutes, granting pain immunity, infinite stamina (unless you have Dodge Expert), immunity to grabs, uncapped strength, and +2 strength. Removes stun-adjacent and stun effects, and can be cast while incapacitated.
Tells you how many mammons someone has on them and in the nervelock.
Tells you how many mammons someone has on them and in the nervelock.

Sacrifice an item in your hand, applying a heal over time to yourself with strength depending on its value.
Create equality, with a thumb on the scales, with your target. Siphon strength, speed, and constitution from them.
Attacks the target by weight of their greed, dealing increased damage and effects depending on how wealthy they are.

Revives the target by invoking a deal with Matthios. In exchange for their lyfe returned, they will be placedin a lasting debt to Him. Any coins within their hands will be spent paying off said debt. Blood for gold.

Fire forth a splinter of unholy bone, tearing flesh and causing bleeding. If you hold pieces of bone in your other hand (or are wearing a zcross around your neck), you will coax a much stronger lance of bone into being, which is capable of severing limbs. 50% stronger versus simple-minded creechers.

Wreath your hand in inhumen energies.
 USE on a mind-inhabited victim who is alyve, floored, whose lux is intact to plunge your hand into their chest, shattering their ribs and will alike in order to forcefully tear the lux from their chest.
 DISARM on a PURE lux to convert it into IMPURE lux, in order to deprive it of those who need it or to fuel your wicked necromantic relics.

Conjure forth a wave of necrotic energy, repelling non-undead around you and greatly damaging their stamina.
Rip the target's soul out of Necra's grasp and revive them at a cost of a humanoid being's heart. The target's attributes will be temporarily reduced.
Summon three spiteful skulls in Zizo's name to harry a chosen foe.
Call forth a towering skeletal aspect of Zizo, granting your foe the only respite she permits.
Fill their throat with profane silence - ensure neither mage-nor-man shall interrupt you, be it invocation or insult.
Woe to the despairing in the face of Ambition. Unleash a cascade of unholy devotion upon the unbeliever - the more devotion they've consumed, the stronger the effect.

The manifestation of the higher concept of a blade itself. Said to be drawn upon from Noc's treasury of wisdom, each casting a poor facsimile of the perfect weapon He once held. This spell requires a Warscholar's mask to be cast.
Recall the form of your treasured Saddleborn mount.
While outside, send your beloved steed away to fend for itself for a time. May take longer in more hostile climates.
Call for your trusty seed, summoning it back to your side after a delay. Only works outdoors. May take longer in more hostile climates.

Metal scales interwoven intricately to form flexible protection!
